headline: Classic 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer' turns 60 Friday. How you can watch this year
fullText:
A Christmas classic turns 60 on Friday, and now's your chance to see it again in the comfort of your home.

The stop-action animation show, "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer," has long been a holiday favorite. The story, centered around life at the North Pole, and the challenges of one outcast reindeer, Rudolph, and his shining red nose, as well as an elf who doesn't fit in and an unsuccessful prospector.

After more than 50 years, the TV special will switch to NBC from its usual host, CBS, with several opportunities to catch "Rudolph" on air throughout December.

If catching the show on broadcast TV doesn't work, you can try streaming, several services offer the classic.

However you plan to watch, get ready to cozy up with a mug of steaming hot chocolate and relish the holiday nostalgia with loved ones this Christmas season.

Here's what to know.

What is 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer'?

"Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" is filmed in stop-motion. The show follows the story of Rudolph, a reindeer at the North Pole, according to IMDb.

Rudolph is ostracized because he was born with a glowing red nose. After running away from home and meeting up with a ragtag group — Hermey the elf, Yukon Cornelius the prospector, a gaggle of misfit toys, and the Abominable Snow Monster — Rudolph returns home to save Christmas using his nose to guide Santa's sleigh through a terrible storm.

Who created Rudolph?

Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer first appeared in 1939 when Montgomery Ward department store asked one of its copywriters, 34-year-old Robert L. May, to create a Christmas story the store could give away to shoppers as a promotional gimmick, according to the Smithsonian. 

The retailer had been buying and giving away coloring books for Christmas every year; and it was decided that creating its own book would save money. In the first year of publication, 2.4 million copies of Rudolph’s story were distributed by Montgomery Ward. 

May’s brother-in-law, songwriter Johnny Marks, decided to adapt the story of Rudolph into song. Marks’ musical version of “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer” was recorded by Gene Autry in 1949. 

More: Christmas TV schedule 2024: Where to watch animated classics like 'Charlie Brown'

When did 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer' premiere?

"Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" premiered on NBC on Dec. 6, 1964.

Who narrated 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer'?

In "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer," the film is narrated by iconic actor Burl Ives, through the guise of Sam the Snowman. He also sang the theme song "Rudolph."

The voice cast also included:

  • Larry D. Mann as Yukon Cornelius and Abominable Snow Monster
  • Billie Mae Richards as Rudolph
  • Paul Soles as Hermey
  • Stan Francis as Santa Claus and King Moonracer
  • Alfie Scopp as Charlie-In-The-Box, Fireball and other reindeer
  • Janis Orenstein as Clarice 
  • Paul Kligman as Donner, Clarice's father, and Comet the coach
  •  Carl Banas as Head Elf, Spotted Elephant and other toys
  • Corinne Conley as Doll and others
  • Peg Dixon as Mrs. Donner, Mrs. Claus and others

More: When should I put up my Christmas tree? Here's what experts say in Michigan

Where will 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer' air on TV?

This season, "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" will air on its home channel of NBC, having moved over from CBS where it aired since the 1970s. The special debuted on NBC in 1964, but switched to CBS in 1971.

When will 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer' air on TV?

"Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" will air on NBC at 8 p.m. Friday, Dec. 6 and at 8 p. m. Thursday, Dec. 12.

It is also part of Freeform's "25 Days of Christmas" lineup, meaning it will air multiple times on the channel. Cable subscribers can catch the classic on Freeform on the following schedule:

  • Dec. 7 at 9:10 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 8 at 6:10 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 16 at 9:20 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 17 at 7:55 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 21 at 6:15 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 22 at 3 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 24 at 8 p.m. ET/PT
  • Dec. 25 at 11 p.m. ET/PT

Where can you stream 'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer'?

"Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" is available to stream on Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+, Google Play and Sling TV.

headline: Holiday cookie walks in metro Detroit: Where to find them
fullText:
Shortbread. Springerle. Spritz.

Cookies abound during the holiday season.        But once the season rolls around, there’s no time for whipping up batches of decorated cookies. And not everyone has the knack or patience.

If dreams of holiday cookies are dancing in your head and there's no time to bake them, take a stroll at one of metro Detroit’s upcoming cookie walks.

Metro area cookie walks are coming up, with most on Dec. 14, though some are this weekend. Thousands of cookie varieties will be up for sale. These events offer a huge assortment of cookies, from classic cutouts to ethnic favorites, most baked by an army of parishioners and volunteers. If you’re unfamiliar with cookie walks, organizers hand out containers or boxes and visitors walk around tables filled with cookies and other sweet treats and choose what they’d like.

What's unique about cookie walks is they offer the chance to customize and choose from a selection of holiday cookies.  

And it's all for a good cause because they help raise funds to support churches, community projects, or other organizations.

The Outreach Ministry's annual cookie walk at Christ Lutheran Church in Sterling Heights is now in its 24th year. Its proceeds have supported many outreach ministries, such as Habitat for Humanity and Adopt-A-Families.

The Sisterhood at Temple Beth El in Bloomfield Township hosts an annual cookie walk, now in its 7th year, that benefits a charitable organization in Detroit's Corktown neighborhood, the Corner Shower and Laundry, a nonprofit that operates out of St. Peter's Episcopal Church.

  • Cookies walks have set hours. It's best to arrive early because goodies sell out fast. People often line up ahead of opening hours.
  • Most cookies, unless noted, are sold by the pound.
  • Typically customers are given a box or container to fill with cookies. Tongs are provided.
  • Other baked goods, candy, and other holiday items decoratively packaged often also sold.
  • Cookies often sell out fast.

headline: Michigan, athletic director Warde Manuel set on 5-year contract extension
fullText:
The University of Michigan and athletic director Warde Manuel have finalized a five-year contract extension.

Manuel's original contract, agreed to on Jan. 29, 2016, was extended in February 2021 to run through June 30, 2026. The new deal will take Manuel through June 30, 2030, according to a release from the school.

“During Warde’s tenure as director, Athletics has put a structure in place where our student-athletes compete for Big Ten and national championships, excel in the classroom, and proudly graduate with their University of Michigan degrees,” Michigan president Santa J. Ono said during U-M's Board of Regents’ meeting Thursday, according to the release.

The school did not release Manual's new salary.

“Every day, I am thankful to work at this great institution and to represent Michigan Athletics," Manuel said in the release. "I especially want to thank the student-athletes, coaches and staff who compete for each of our teams and who have helped us achieve unparalleled success athletically and academically. I am excited to continue giving back to a university that has provided me with so much over my career.”

Manuel was hired to run his alma mater's athletic department in 2016 after a near four-year run at the University of Connecticut.

Manuel, 56, was a defensive end at U-M in the 1980s under Bo Schembechler and is the 12th athletic director in Michigan history. He has served as a member of the College Football Playoff selection committee since 2022 and became chair of the committee ahead of the 2024 football season.

Manuel was also announced as the 2024 recipient of the National Football Foundation's John L. Toner Award, which "recognizes athletics directors who have demonstrated superior administrative abilities and shown outstanding dedication to college athletics, particularly college football" earlier this summer and is set to be honored in Las Vegas next week.

SABIN: In firing Kirk Campbell and landing Bryce Underwood, it's a new era for Michigan football

Under Manuel's watch, the Wolverines have won national championships in football (2023) and women's gymnastics (2021), and finished as runners-up in wrestling (2022), field hockey (2020), baseball (2019), men's basketball (2018) and women's cross country (2017).

Michigan athletes have won 23 individual NCAA titles during his tenure, 85 regular-season and tournament conference titles, 61 Academic All-American honors, 535 Big Ten distinguished scholar nods, and more than 3,500 Academic All-Big Ten honors.

Manuel signed a contract in February of 2021 starting effective March 14, 2021, that his base salary would go to $1.1 million for the next 12 months. The most recent numbers show that Manuel's salary was $1,227,100, according to a salary book published annually by the university, which was distributed on Dec. 8 of last year.

According to Manuel's latest contract, he was also eligible for as much as $150,000 in incentives while the university would contribute $350,000 each year to a retirement plan. The numbers on this latest contract figure to go up, and not only because he is on the heels of a football national title, the basketball program is ranked for the first time in two years and the No. 1 high school football player in America signed to play in Ann Arbor on Wednesday.

In addition, extensions for ADs have been the trend in the league recently. Deals have been re-done in the league just this year by Penn State, Maryland, Wisconsin, UCLA, Indiana and Minnesota.

That's not to mention Troy Dannen taking over at Nebraska — his annual base pay is $1.6 million, but he got a $1 million signing bonus, while Nebraska agreed to pay the $1.5 million he owed previous employer Washington (which then poached rival Washington State AD Pat Chun). Or Ohio State, where Ross Bjork took over for long-time AD Gene Smith: he is making essentially $2 million in basic annual compensation, with $1.65 million base salary and $350,000 for media, promotions and public relations.

Tennessee's Danny White is the nation's highest paid athletic director, at $2.75 million, though Texas’ Chris Del Conte is closing in, now that he's reaching the part of his back-loaded contract which is higher in AAV.

In Ann Arbor, Manuel's tenure hasn't been without its scrutiny.

ONE-ON-ONE WITH U-M'S WARDE MANUEL: Addressing football controversies, past missteps

He saw significant backlash from the fanbase after he handed former head coach Jim Harbaugh a three-game suspension to begin last season, then got even more pushback from the program's supporters when they felt he didn't do enough to offer Harbaugh a new contract before he left in January to coach the Los Angeles Chargers.

Michigan football also remains under investigation by the NCAA for an an alleged sign-stealing scheme that involved former staffer Connor Stalions; a response to the notice of allegations was due two weeks ago but those around Michigan are mum, per advice from U-M attorneys.

The football program is already on probation the next three years and will face other penalties from the NCAA due to violations during a COVID-19 dead period and for having noncoaching staff members participate in impermissible roles under former coach Jim Harbaugh.

At other times on Manuel's watch he has had to answer for scandal in the hockey department under Mel Pearson, explain why a former star point guard crashed a car registered to Manuel's family and then misidentified himself to police, and defended former basketball coach Juwan Howard, who got into physical and verbal altercations on multiple occasions, with members of his staff and other teams.

All the while, Manuel has had remarkable success across each of his programs. From 2020-24 U-M as an institution has 52 Big Ten championships. The next closest competition in the conference is Ohio State, who has 28.

U-M has also finished top six in the LEARFIELD Directors' Cup standings five times during Manuel's tenure.

*USA Today Sports Projects Reporter Steve Berkowitz contributed to this report

This story was updated to reflect Michigan's announcement of the extension.

Tony Garcia is the Michigan Wolverines beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia.

headline: Michigan law now requires drivers to stay 200 feet from snowplows — or face fines
fullText:
With Michigan winter firmly in place, lawmakers have passed legislation aimed at preventing crashes with snowplows.

Drivers who fail to provide snowplows and salt truck enough space could face fines.

During the 2022-23 winter season there were 30,786 winter weather crashes, according to the Michigan State Police, including 59 fatal crashes.

Legislation that is now in effect is intended to reduce those numbers. Here's what to know about the new law to keep drivers safe:

What does Michigan law say about snowplows?

The Michigan law signed by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer in July says drivers must stay 200 feet behind a snowplow unless they are passing.

Michigan drivers can be no closer than 20 feet away from the truck that is stopped at an intersection.

What is a snowplow?

Snowplows includes vehicles that are:

  • Operating on behalf of the state, a county or county road commission, or a municipality.
  • Actively engaging in snow and ice removal, snowplowing, salting or sanding.

What happens if I get too close to a plow?

Drivers who don't stay far enough away from plows are guilty of a civil infraction with a fine $100.

Rules of the road in Michigan

  • Drivers are allowed to pass snowplows on the left. Most snowplow/ vehicle crashes occur when passenger vehicles hit snowplows from behind or while attempting to pass, the state police say, and caution drivers to avoid passing.
  • When meeting a snowplow coming from the opposite direction, slow down and increase your distance from the centerline.
  • Snowplows are considered authorized vehicles, a part of the Michigan Move Over Law meaning vehicles must move over and slow to 10 mph below the posted speed limit when they see them in their rearview mirror.

How to see what Michigan roads are clear

MI Drive, an online tool from the Michigan Department of Transportation allows residents to see which roads have been recently plowed including special event and future road closures. Michigan drivers can also find a wealth of other safety information on the website.

headline: Rare snow doughnuts, a unique phenomenon, appear in west Michigan backyard
fullText:
As West Michigan was whipped with winter weather and lake-effect snows Wednesday, Paw Paw residents Janice and Eric Pantelleria went outside to find some unusual lawn ornaments: dozens upon dozens of nicely rolled-up snow doughnuts or cylinders across their large lawn.

The snowy rollers are a somewhat unusual weather phenomenon, said Megan Varcie, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in White Lake.

"You had this kind of heavy, sticky snow coming off the lake that packed together well, combined with heavy winds — West Michigan had wind gusts upward of 40 mph," she said. "In those conditions, these cylindrical snow rolls can form, especially in open areas without trees."

"My husband was outside clearing the driveway when he noticed them," Janice Pantelleria said. "At first he thought that the kids had rolled a couple snowballs in the yard — but then noticed that they were surrounding our house."

Pantelleria's photos of the snow rolls were shared on Facebook, and received plenty of attention.

More: Lake effect snow blankets part of Michigan every year. Here's where and what to know

"I'm glad everyone is enjoying the photos as much as we enjoyed seeing it firsthand," Janice Pantelleria said.

headline: Detroit Lions kicker Jake Bates named NFC Special Teams Player of the Month
fullText:
Jake Bates' first NFL season keeps getting better.

Bates, the Detroit Lions' first-year kicker, was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Month on Thursday after leading the NFC with 41 points scored in November.

Bates made 8 of 9 field-goal tries and all 17 of his extra points in five November games as the Lions went undefeated in the month. He made the game-winning 52-yarder as time expired in a Week 10 win over the Houston Texans and was 4-for-4 on 50-plus-yard kicks in November.

Bates is the third Lion to win a Player of the Month award this season.

Aidan Hutchinson was NFC Defensive Player of the Month after registering 6½ sacks in September, and Jared Goff was NFC Offensive Player of the Month after posting a 149.8 passer rating in October.

The Lions enter December on a 10-game winning streak and with an NFC-best 11-1 record. They host the Green Bay Packers Thursday in a game that could go a long way towards determining the No. 1 seed in conference for the playoffs.

The Lions currently lead the Philadelphia Eagles (10-2) and Minnesota Vikings (10-2) by one game in division, but would lose the common-opponent tiebreaker to the Eagles if they lost to the Packers and both teams finished with 15-2 records.

Bates is 19-for-20 on field goals this season. He missed a kick for the first time in his career last week in the Lions' 23-20 Thanksgiving win over the Chicago Bears.

headline: Patrick Kane cleared to return —now Detroit Red Wings need him back in last season's form
fullText:
Patrick Kane is cleared for a return to the lineup for the Detroit Red Wings — and now they need him to be back like last season's version.

Kane, 36, had missed five straight games on injured reserve because of an upper-body injury when he was cleared Thursday morning to return. Coach Derek Lalonde told reporters in Ottawa that Kane would be back in the lineup, and that Joe Veleno would come out.

Kane's availability was much needed for the Wings, who had put Tyler Motte — a journeyman with one goal in 13 games this season — into the top six during Kane's absence.

BUSY FEBRUARY BREAK: Detroit Red Wings Dylan Larkin, Lucas Raymond headed to 4 Nations Face-Off tournament

Kane had three goals and seven assists for 10 points in 20 games prior to his injury, well below the impact he made last season when he joined the Wings coming off invasive hip surgery.

The Wings re-signed Kane over the summer for one year at $4 million because he added so much to their lineup, coming in cold last December and finishing with 20 goals and 27 points in 50 games, just a touch below a point-per-game performance.

Kane came into this season having had a full summer to work out, and being with the Wings from training camp. But his struggles have mirrored that of the team: Mediocre performances, with occasional flashes of what might be.

There's no questioning Kane's hockey smarts: He's a lock to make the Hockey Hall of Fame on the first ballot, and six points from becoming the second American with 1,300 points in the NHL. But he has not had the same impact on the Wings this season as last, because the Wings have not been the same as last.

The Wings have struggled to rise above mediocrity, but Kane's return will at least restore balance to the top six, and in that way, also strengthen the entire lineup.

headline: Expanding FOIA laws to Michigan governor, lawmakers could fizzle in lame-duck
fullText:
LANSING — While Michigan's Democratic lawmakers rush to move their policy priorities to the finish line during the final days of the legislative session, one big bipartisan proposal that has stalled for years could die or fly during lame duck: Bills to subject lawmakers and the governor to public records requests.

Michigan is one of two states without public records laws that cover the state legislature and governor's office, and Senate Majority Leader Winnie Brinks, D-Grand Rapids, would like to end Michigan's status as a national outlier.

The Michigan Senate has already passed bills to expand the state's Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) with wide bipartisan support. FOIA laws allow the public to access information about the government by obtaining a range of records, from officials' communications to police reports. State and local offices are already subject to FOIA in Michigan but state lawmakers and the governors' offices are not.

Bills that would change that have stalled in the Michigan House. House Speaker Joe Tate, D-Detroit — who decides which bills come to the House floor for a vote — said he's open to the legislation. But Tate declined to say whether he'd vote yes on the FOIA bills when asked in an interview with the Detroit Free Press Wednesday.

For years, Michigan lawmakers have introduced bills to improve government transparency by expanding the state's public records laws. But they went nowhere. This year, lawmakers in the state Senate advanced bills and voted on them.

Several transparency advocates testified in support of the bills during a committee hearing in February. "Openness and transparency are pillars of a strong democracy, but Michiganders are currently restricted from viewing key information that would illustrate the vital function that you serve, and that the governor’s office serves: How policy is shaped," Kim Murphy-Kovalick from Voters Not Politicians told lawmakers. Those supporting the legislation raised concerns about some of the exemptions for disclosing certain information but described the bills as a strong start.

Brinks said in an interview Wednesday that she'd be proud to make increasing government transparency part of the legacy lawmakers leave behind during lame duck before Republicans are set to take control of the state House next year. "I think there is bipartisan support in (the state House) maybe now that the dynamic has changed a little bit I think you might see a greater — I'm certainly hopeful that you'll see a greater — willingness on the part of the House Republicans to put votes up on things that they believe are the right things to do regardless of whether or not House Dems have every single one of their members up on the board as a yes."

Michigan Legislature: What will Michigan's lame duck session look like? 'Everything is on the table'

Shortly after Republicans in November chose Minority Leader Matt Hall, R-Richland Township, to serve as House Speaker starting next year, Hall noted his support for expanding FOIA in the past. "I'm not sure how serious the Democrats are about that. We saw them talk about it for years and then they don't take action. Isn't that interesting? I will tell you this though ... what I intend to do is work with our team to reform how the budget's done. I think that's an issue of transparency. I'll say I feel more passionately about that," he told reporters last month.

When she first ran for governor, Whitmer released a transparency plan telling voters that she supported expanding FOIA to include the governor's office and legislature. She vowed to take action if lawmakers wouldn't and use her authority to extend FOIA to the lieutenant governor and governor's offices. She hasn't done so.

Whitmer press secretary Stacey LaRouche did not say whether Whitmer wants to see the FOIA bills land on the governor's desk before the end of the year. LaRouche said Whitmer has taken steps to advance government transparency in Michigan such as an executive directive signed in 2019 calling for the appointment of a transparency liaison at state agencies and encouraging livestreamed public meetings. "We will review legislation as it makes its way through the process," LaRouche said in an email.

Whitmer told the Free Press in a June interview she'd still like to see the FOIA legislation passed. "But when the Legislature's ready to, you know, have it apply to both branches, I think we'll have something to sign," she said. "I think we've got an opportunity and a duty to get something done. I also know we're in probably the last four or five weeks of the term for quite awhile and there's a lot to do. So not that I'm saying it can't get done, it could. But you know there's a lot on the list between now and July 1," Whitmer said.

Lawmakers find themselves in a similar situation in lame duck, staring down a long list of priorities. And the clock is ticking on whether expanding FOIA will be part of the legacy the first Democratic trifecta in Michigan in 40 years will leave.

headline: Dearborn police distributing free drug and alcohol testing kits to concerned parents
fullText:
The Dearborn Police Department is distributing free drug testing kits for parents worried their children may be using illicit substances.

The Parental Evaluation Resource Kits (PERK) include a 5-panel drug and alcohol test and a nicotine test to use at home. The tests provide immediate results.

Also included in the kits: information about local resources, like the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS) and Leaders Advancing and Helping Communities (LAHC), according to Dearborn police.

“PERK evaluation kits are a private, convenient first step to ease the anxiety and uncertainty for parents who suspect their child may be involved in risky behavior and is using dangerous substances," Dearborn Police Chief Issa Shahin said in a statement.

"As we remain committed to the health and safety of our youth, we also encourage constant communication with family members along with other professional resources.”

More: Demolition set for Detroit's Mammoth building, but owners are not done fighting

More: Prosecutor: Waterford man gave human trafficking victims crack to keep them up for days

Dearborn police describe PERK as preventative and a first step for parents, guardians or other family members with children showing signs of illicit drug usage.

But Dearborn police said PERK is not meant to diagnose substance abuse disorders and may not be the most effective way to determine if a child is engaging in substance abuse.

If substance abuse is expected, Dearborn police encourage families to reach out to licensed substance abuse counselors or other related resources. For more information, families can call the Dearborn Police Department at 313-943-2241.

headline: Alfred Talley, pioneering fast-food executive and longtime Southfield resident, dies at 94
fullText:
Alfred Talley, a longtime Detroit area resident who held multiple leadership positions in the fast-food industry at companies such as Jack in the Box and KFC, has died at the age of 94.

Talley died on Nov. 10, his daughter, Patricia Talley, confirmed. A cause of death was not given.

Patricia Talley described her dad as a "pioneer" in the fast-food industry. He was named executive vice president of Foodmaker Inc., which was then the operator and franchiser of the fast-food chain of Jack in the Box restaurants, in the late 1960s, she said, which made him among the very first African American in the U.S. to be elevated to a corporate management level in the fast-food restaurant industry.

Later, when he became the franchisee district manager for the eastern Michigan region for KFC and a franchisee, with stores in New Baltimore and Marysville, he received the fast-food restaurant chain's "Five Star Operator Award."

Talley's interest in operations extended beyond his career to his personal life, and even to his own death. Patricia Talley said her father gave her an "operations manual" on what to do after he died, which included the story of his life, which was shared with the Detroit Free Press.

Talley, the youngest of five children, was born in Pennsylvania on Sept. 1, 1930, and moved to Detroit in 1931 when his father died.

He attended Detroit Public Schools, graduating from Pershing High School in 1948. He later earned a Bachelor of Science in business management and supervision from Central Michigan University.

He married his childhood sweetheart, Barbara Wall, in 1949.

After working for the Detroit Department of Street Railways, he moved his family to Los Angeles in 1961 and began his career as a lessee-manager of three Jack in the Box restaurants. He was promoted several times and went on to become Foodmaker Inc.'s executive vice president, Talley wrote in the story of his life.

It was in Los Angeles that the Talley family experienced racist incidents, such as when they put several offers in to buy a house and the real estate agent said the owner would not sell to them because they were Black and they would ruin the neighborhood, his wife, Barbara, wrote in a post for the publication "United Methodist Insight."

Talley went on to hold several leadership positions at different companies and eventually moved back to the Detroit area, to Southfield.

The housing discrimination the Talley family faced is what fueled Talley's passion for civil rights, Southfield Mayor Ken Siver, who was a neighbor of the Talley family for many years, said in an email.

Siver said when the Talleys moved to Southfield in the 1970s, they were "poised for a similar experience (as LA) and found the opposite." They were among the first African Americans to move to that community, he said.

When he moved back to the Detroit area, Talley established his own restaurant company, Burger Giant Restaurants, with seven restaurants in Detroit. He eventually dissolved that company after several robberies at the restaurants and the pressure of competing with national fast-food chains, according to the story he wrote about his life.

Talley's last job in the restaurant industry before retiring was as a franchisee district manager for KFC's eastern Michigan region and a franchisee, with restaurants in New Baltimore and Marysville.

He sold his KFCs in 1990 and retired. After Talley retired, he worked part time as a golf starter for the city of Southfield.

Siver said Alfred and Barbara — who he said was Southfield's first African American city councilwoman — also became very involved in civic affairs since moving to Southfield.

"Together, they were a strong force in the city," Siver said.

More: William Roberts, longtime mayor of Walled Lake, remembered for public service, dedication

Barbara Talley founded the Southfield Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Task Force, a nonprofit dedicated to promoting social justice, nonviolence and equality, 40 years ago. Siver said that the organization hosted Michigan's first and largest MLK celebration and will host a 40th celebration on Jan. 20.

A funeral is planned for 12 p.m. Friday at Hope United Methodist Church in Southfield. The service will be livestreamed on the church’s YouTube channel and Facebook page.

headline: Michigan football's next offensive coordinator: Four possible candidates
fullText:
The Michigan football program has the nation's top quarterback recruit coming to join the offense next season.

But who'll be calling the plays for Bryce Underwood (or whoever starts at QB for the Wolverines)?

Michigan head coach Sherrone Moore fired offensive coordinator Kirk Campbell earlier this week, saying even after the high of a 13-10 win over Ohio State, he had to be honest with himself in assessing the offense's performance in Campbell's first year.

It was one of the worst offensive seasons in the modern era in Ann Arbor, as U-M finished No. 128 out of 133 FBS-level teams in total offense (294.2 yards per game), No. 130 in passing (113.6 yards), and tied for No. 114 in scoring (22.3 points).

“Unfortunately had to make a change and thought that was the best direction we had to go,” Moore told reporters Wednesday. “But offensively, I want to be explosive in the run and the pass and balanced. That’s as much as I’ll give you right now. Going through that process of candidates and we’ll find the best one that fits us and fits this program that wants to be at Michigan.

NEW DEAL: Michigan, athletic director Warde Manuel finalizing 5-year contract extension

"We want to be a balanced team ... we’ve still got to be able to run the football, that’s got to be a thing to do. But someone that’s going to develop the quarterback at a high rate and put them in a great position. Obviously, we’ve got to be able to teach a young guy, whether he starts Day 1, Week 2, Year 2, whatever it is. When you’ve got to develop them, you’ve got to see the progress. As far as what the offense will look like, that’ll take shape as we go.”

Instantly, U-M becomes one of the more coveted jobs in the sport, featuring a top prospect and a winning pedigree.

So where will Moore look?

Will it be someone like his defensive coordinator, Wink Martindale, with decades of NFL experience to come and bring a professional mindset? Or another up-and-coming mind — like Campbell was considered to be when promoted earlier this year — but perhaps just a better fit at a better time?

It sounds like Moore wants both.

“There are guys that are both,” Moore said. “There are guys that have done it. There are guys that have been head coaches. There are guys that have been coordinators. There are guys that are coordinators now that haven’t done it as long.

“There’s a vast mix of a group of guys. So, we’ll just keep chopping away and trying to find the best guy.”

Here are four candidates Moore could consider.

Dan Mullen

Résumé: Studio analyst, ABC/ESPN; former Florida, Mississippi State head coach.

The buzz: He has been a head coach in the SEC for 13 years so there's little concern about any qualifications here.

Mullen, who went 103-61 (54-53 in league play) in SEC jobs with Mississippi State (69-46 from 2009-17) and Florida (34-15 from 2018-21), has spent the past few years covering college football for ABC and ESPN but could be itching to get back into the game. Two of his squads (Florida in 2018-19) finished in the top 10 of the polls; he also led Mississippi State to three seasons finishing in the polls.

But Mullen is best known for his work as an offensive assistant, developed under the tutelage of Urban Meyer. He was Meyer's quarterbacks coach in Bowling Green (2001-02) and Utah (2003-04) before joining him in Florida and adding the offensive coordinator title to his job (2005-08) as Meyer led the Gators to two national championships. Mullen has led QB rooms with Tim Tebow and Dak Prescott, so Underwood would presumably be in good hands.

Joe Sloan

Résumé: LSU offensive coordinator.

The buzz: This would be twisting the metaphorical knife, as the Tigers were set to bring Underwood into Sloan's offense before the Belleville product flipped to U-M in November, but the rationale here is clear: Underwood clearly had a very good relationship with the staff in Baton Rouge. Nothing seemed to sour on that end.

Would U-M really try and bully a legitimate SEC power and poach its play-caller, too? Sloan, 37, has only been at the Power Four level for three years but is already considered one of the hottest young coaching minds in the sport. He led Jayden Daniels, in his only LSU season, to a Heisman Trophy a year ago; this year, Garrett Nussmeier is having a nice season, completing 63.7% of his passes for 3,739 yards, 26 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. (For comparison's sake, all U-M quarterbacks have combined for 10 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 2024.)

Joe Craddock

Résumé: Tulane offensive coordinator.

The buzz: Beyond Craddock's work for the Green Wave, he has some additional buzz, as Fox's Bruce Feldman reported last Saturday that not only was Campbell likely to be fired, but that Craddock could be a potential replacement.

Still only 39, Craddock already has experience as an offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at SMU (2015-17), Arkansas (2018-19), Troy (2022-23) and Tulane, following a start at Clemson.

Craddock's offense this season in New Orleans was fairly balanced — he called 52% runs and 48% passes for Tulane —but the run game was far more successful, ranking No. 12 (212.9 yards per game) nationally, while the pass game was No. 81 in passing (216.4 yards per game). Still, that was enough for the Green Wave to finish the regular season No. 34 in total offense (439.3) and, most importantly, No. 6 in scoring (39.1 points per game) entering Friday's AAC championship game.

Jason Candle

Résumé: Toledo head coach.

The buzz: Anytime you're doing well as a MAC coach, your name is going to get floated around for coordinator positions in the Big Ten. Heck, Candle was perceived as a legitimate candidate by some for the Michigan State head coach opening last year.

Candle, 45, has turned Toledo into a consistent winner, going 72-40 with seven bowl berths, three MAC West Division crowns, two MAC championships and two nods as MAC Coach of the Year (2017, 2023) in nine seasons since he took over for the final game of the 2015 season (following Matt Campbell's hiring by Iowa State). He was the offensive coordinator for the Rockets before that, so it may be tough to pry him from a program where he has spent the past 16 years. Candle likes to run a power-spread offense and found plenty of success from 2021-23 with former Detroit King quarterback DeQuan Finn, in the same mold as Underwood.

And, of course, Toledo is right between Ann Arbor and Columbus, Ohio, giving Candle familiarity with the area and strong recruiting ties already. Adding a national brand behind that could tip the scales in U-M's direction even further.

headline: Matt Patricia: 'Give credit to Dan Campbell' for Lions' rebuild. Did he mean it?
fullText:
A few months after legendary former New England Patriots coach Bill Belichick gave former Detroit Lions coach Matt Patricia credit for laying the groundwork for Dan Campbell's current success, Patricia is taking a different approach.

Belichick said in September the Lions are enjoying "the fruits of the labor from" Patricia, referencing the Lions' dominant offensive line that has holdovers from the Patricia-Bob Quinn era.

When Patricia was asked about his former team Thursday, he said Dan Campbell deserves credit for getting buy-in across the building, but did he also take a little credit for having the vision along the way?

GUYS GETTING HURT LIKE CRAZY: Detroit Lions keep winning despite injuries. But are they close to a breaking point?

In an appearance on "Good Morning Football" on NFL Network, Patricia was asked about the players who are still on the team from his time, and took the opportunity to highlight center Frank Ragnow, the Lions' first-round pick in 2018, while talking about his belief that "you build the team from the center out."

"I go right to Frank Ragnow, just because that's so personal to me," Patricia said. "That was my first draft pick, you know, sitting there Round 1 and you're looking before the draft and trying to figure out who's going to be on the board, I think we were like 15 or somewhere in the mid-first round and I just loved him.

"He was an offensive lineman, he was a center, I played center, and he was just smart, tough and you could just see, if we build the team from the ball out, you know start at the ball and build it out, start with the center position and it was Frank Ragnow."

It's the last part that fans appear to be latching onto, which sounds like Patricia taking credit for the vision of building through the line. It's a strategy which has paid off immensely, but not exactly in the way Patricia may like to remember.

Three members of the Lions' current offensive line were on the team when Patricia was in Detroit: Ragnow, Taylor Decker and Graham Glasgow. However, Glasgow and Decker were drafted by Quinn while Patricia was still the Patriots' defensive coordinator, and Quinn and Patricia later allowed Glasgow to leave as a free agent after Patricia's second season. Two years later, the Lions and new general manager Brad Holmes spent their first-round pick (No. 7 overall) on Oregon's Penei Sewell, who is arguably the catalyst for much of what the Lions do on the O-line now.

Patricia was also asked about why the team has taken the next step since he left, and that's when he gave a shoutout to Campbell.

"Give credit to Dan Campbell and what he was able to do to just get the entire building to follow what he wanted them to do, believe in what they were preaching, go out, work hard," Patricia said.

"Sometimes it just needs a little bit of a spark, a little bit of belief and we've seen that in individual guys who go out and all the sudden you make a play and you become a great player in the league. It's no different with a team."

Patricia was fired as head coach of the Detroit Lions during the 2020 season when the Lions were just 4-7 and 13-29-1 in total under his watch.

Both Patricia and Quinn were let go after multiple unsuccessful seasons together, and the Lions eventually hired Campbell in January 2021, pairing him with Holmes, and the rest is (franchise) history.

The Lions enter Thursday's showdown with the Green Bay Packers winners of 10 straight games and in the driver's seat in the NFC if they can stay perfect the rest of the way.

headline: Lions vs. Packers score: Recap, highlights from Lions' playoff-clinching win over Packers
fullText:
The Detroit Lions started December with a pivotal NFC North matchup at home and walked away with a playoff spot clinched on a last-second kick.

The Lions (12-1) outlasted the Green Bay Packers (9-4), 34-31, in a back-and-forth heavyweight battle on a game-winning kick from Jake Bates on the final snap of the game. The lead changed hands constantly in the second half, but Detroit had the ball last and walked away with the win.

The Lions won a franchise-record 11th straight game by beating the Packers on Thursday night to become the first team in the NFC to secure a spot in the postseason and a season sweep over their divisional rivals. The Lions beat the Packers at Lambeau Field just over a month ago in the first matchup and got its first sweep over Green Bay since 2022.

Detroit has now won a franchise-record 11 straight games to maintain first place in the NFC and have firm control of the No.1 seed entering the final four weeks of the regular season. The Packers are three games behind Detroit in the division and had a three-game winning streak snapped.

The Lions and Packers are tied at 31 late in the fourth quarter. Detroit marched down the field on the opening drive and finished with a David Montgomery touchdown. The defense kept Green Bay in check until their final drive of the half, where they ran all over Detroit and finished with a Josh Jacobs touchdown. But Detroit responded with a touchdown pass to Jahmyr Gibbs just before halftime.

Green Bay opened the second half with a touchdown to Tucker Kraft after a deep shot, and got an interception immediately after. Jacobs scored his second touchdown to put the Packers ahead, and the Lions answered with a long scoring drive ending with a Tim Patrick touchdown. The Lions failed on fourth down in their own territory to finish the third quarter, leading to a third Jacobs touchdown, but Detroit found another answer with Patrick's second touchdown catch to go up by 3. The Packers tied it with a short field goal with less than four minutes left.

The Lions used up the remaining 3:38 to reach field goal position, including a gutsy fourth-and-1 conversion from Green Bay's 21-yard line instead of just kicking, to set up a game-winning kick from Jake Bates as time expired. Bates now has two winning kicks for the Lions this year, and his first at Ford Field since he played for the Michigan Panthers.

Defensive tackle Alim McNeill was ruled out after halftime with a head injury. He left after the Lions' fourth defensive snap to be checked for a concussion but came back in during the second quarter before leaving again at halftime. Safety Brian Branch left in the fourth quarter and is questionable to return with calf cramping.

REQUIRED READING: Detroit Lions keep winning despite injuries. But are they close to a breaking point?

With a win, the Lions clinched a playoff spot with four weeks left and maintained a lead over the Minnesota Vikings, Philadelphia Eagles and Packers at the top of the NFC. Detroit is now 4-0 against the NFC North this season.

Check out the recap from the Lions-Packers battle on Thursday night below.

Lions vs. Packers game recap, highlights

3:38, 4Q: Packers tie game at 31 with late 32-yard FG

The Thursday night drama has reached its climax.

Detroit will get the ball back with less than four minutes with a tie score after the Packers marched down and tied it with a 32-yard field goal by Brandon McManus. The drive got kickstarted with a 29-yard completion to Christian Watson, followed by 26 and 12-yard completions to Dontayvion Wicks to reach the red zone. On second-and-goal, the Packers seemingly scored, but Watson was called for offensive pass interference for setting a basketball screen on Kerby Joseph in coverage, and Ezekiel Turner pulled down a scrambling Jordan Love on third down to force a field goal.

8:39, 4Q: Tim Patrick scores 2nd TD to put Lions ahead 31-28

The whiplash hasn't stopped as the Lions found another answer to re-take the lead.

Detroit drove 70 yards in 10 plays, ending with Jared Goff faking a handoff on third-and-goal from the 2 and turning and firing to Patrick on a backside slant for his second touchdown in Detroit and of the game. The Lions started the drive with an 18-yard completion to Patrick over the middle, followed by 11 yards to Amon-Ra St. Brown and a 17-yard completion to a diving Sam LaPorta to reach scoring range. The Lions ran a fake sweep counter reverse to St. Brown to reach the red zone, and then turned to David Montgomery to reach the goal line and set up a touchdown pass.

14:20, 4Q: Josh Jacobs scores 3rd TD; Lions trail 28-24

The failed fourth down proved to be costly for the Lions. The Packers picked up 21 yards on a completion over the middle to Tucker Kraft and then Jacobs lowered his head and carried a pile four yards into the end zone for his third touchdown to give Green Bay the lead again late.

1:29, 3Q: Lions fail on 4th down in own territory

After successfully gambling on the first three fourth-down conversions, the fourth one went Green Bay's way. The Lions forced a punt and were about to go three-and-out right back, but kept the offense on the field for fourth-and-1 from their own 31. They ran Gibbs far to the right, but Green Bay was ready for it and tackled him behind the line of scrimmage for a turnover on downs to take over already in scoring position.

5:04, 3Q: Lions re-take 24-21 lead on Tim Patrick 4th down TD

The Lions found another answer for the Packers' punch coming out of the locker room. Detroit put together a 13-play, 70-yard drive that ended with Jared Goff hitting an open Patrick on a hitch at the goal line on fourth-and-goal from the 3-yard line for his first touchdown as a Lion. The drive started with Jared Goff converting a fourth-and-1 with a quarterback sneak at midfield, followed by two first-down gains from David Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs to reach scoring range. The Lions picked up five more yards before having to find a way to convert on fourth down with a pass to Patrick.

12:29, 3Q: Jared Goff intercepted by Keisean Nixon, Josh Jacobs scores 3 plays later; Lions trail 21-17

The Lions' first turnover put Green Bay in a position to take the lead for the first time. After a holding penalty set Detroit back, Goff tried to fit a pass into a tight window to Tim Patrick, but Nixon was right there and jumped in front for an interception and returned it to the Lions' 16-yard line.

Three plays later, Josh Jacobs carried a pile of players into the end zone to give Green Bay the lead.

13:15, 3Q: Packers open 2nd half with Tucker Kraft TD; Lions lead 17-14

The Packers opted to open up and attack deep to start the second half. On the second play, Jordan Love fired a deep shot to Christian Watson, who beat Carlton Davis cleanly 1-on-1, for a 59-yard gain to reach Detroit's 12 immediately. After two incomplete passes, Love fit a pass into a tight window past Davis to Tucker Kraft, who used his big frame to wrangle the contested catch.

Halftime: Jared Goff hits Jahmyr Gibbs for 4th down TD to take 17-7 lead

The Lions took the final five minutes off the clock and answered Green Bay's touchdown with one of their own to re-establish a 10-point lead. The Lions reached the 4-yard line with a completion to Sam LaPorta, and then ran down to the 1-yard line. Jared Goff ran a quarterback sneak on second-and-goal and initially got a touchdown, but replay showed he was short, and David Montgomery got stuffed on third down. The Lions ran a spread set with three tight ends and Tim Patrick on the field, and flooded the flats while Gibbs cooked a linebacker with a Texas route for a wide-open touchdown over the middle with 10 seconds left in the half.

Through the first 30 minutes, the Lions have outgained the Packers 174-104 and have converted 4-of-8 third-down attempts and a fourth-down attempt while Green Bay is 0-for-2 on third downs. Green Bay will open the second half with the ball.

5:35, 2Q: Packers get on board with Josh Jacobs TD; Lions lead 10-7

The Packers went to the ground and didn't stop for their first points of the game, with a little bit of help from the Lions' defensive penalties. Green Bay drove 70 yards in 11 plays, only completing one pass, with a smashmouth style that picked up 60 rushing yards with 10 carries. Detroit had three defensive penalties on the drive, including two in the red zone, that were back-breakers and gave the Packers extra chances. On third-and-goal from the 5, Terrion Arnold was too physical against Christian Watson to force an eventual tipped interception, drawing a pass interference penalty and setting up the touchdown a play later. The Packers have 81 rushing yards on 13 carries for an average of over 6 yards per carry.

13:01, 2Q: Jake Bates hits 43-yard FG; Lions lead 10-0

The Lions turned the fumble recovery into points, but couldn't sustain a drive to the end zone. The Lions went 29 yards in six plays to set up a 43-yard field goal from Bates, who bounced back after missing his first NFL field goal last week against the Bears. The Lions picked up a first down with a 10-yard completion to Sam LaPorta, followed by a personal foul against Packers linebacker Quay Walker for a late hit against Dan Skipper to reach field goal range. Detroit got stuffed on a run and missed on an attempted pass to Jameson Williams to kill the drive.

14:50, 2Q: Carlton Davis forces Christian Watson fumble, David Long recovers

The Lions defense produced the first turnover of the game on the opening play of the second quarter. Jordan Love withstood pressure from a blitz up the middle and delivered a perfect pass to a wide open Watson on a crossing route. Watson took off down the sideline for what seemed to be a big gain, but ended up losing the ball fighting for extra yards. Watson tried to leap Kerby Joseph, who upended him, and Davis came in to knock the ball loose just before Watson hit the ground, and Long scooped up the loose ball near midfield.

0:35, 1Q: Lions, Packers trade punts

The Packers picked up one first down but had to punt after the Lions generated pressure on third down to force an off-base throw from Jordan Love. Detroit responded with a prompt three-and-out but held Green Bay to a punt after giving them starting field position at midfield. The Lions were able to get out of the shadow of its goal posts a bit, but eventually had to settle for another punt from Jack Fox. Green Bay has it at its own 17 to start their third drive.

9:41, 1Q: Lions take 7-0 lead on David Montgomery TD on opening drive

The Lions wanted the opening kickoff, and it proved to be for good reason. Detroit drove 70 yards in 11 plays and found the end zone on a 3-yard touchdown run from David Montgomery after the Lions earned an extra set of downs thanks to a Packers illegal contact penalty on third-and-goal. Detroit converted two third downs on the drive with completions to Amon-Ra St. Brown in the flat and Jameson Williams to keep the drive alive. Montgomery had three carries for 18 yards, while Jared Goff completed six of eight passes for 58 yards. The Lions opted to attack early and often through the air, and only had one setback on a holding penalty against Dan Skipper.

Barry Sanders meets the Grinch; Tarik Skubal at Ford Field

Yes, that headline is correct. The Hall of Fame Lions' running back got a chance to meet the biggest threat to Christmas somewhere at Ford Field pregame as part of the special primetime festivities during the holiday season. Also, Detroit Tigers ace and AL Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal was in the building either rocking a custom 29 jersey or supporting Kindle Vildor as his fellow No. 29 wearer.

Lions injury report: Moseley out 2nd straight game, Jamal Adams active

The Lions' pregame injury report only had one surprise: cornerback Emmanuel Moseley is inactive for the second straight game. He was joined by offensive linemen Giovanni Manu and Colby Sorsdal and the four injured starting linemen — left tackle Taylor Decker, defensive ends Josh Paschal and Levi Onwuzurike and defensive tackle D.J. Reader. Detroit's two newest defenders, Jamal Adams and Kwon Alexander, are active for their Lions' debut.

Lions defenders arrive for TNF

Za'Darius Smith and Terrion Arnold both arrived at Ford Field in a matching fit from head to toe. Smith showed up for the matchup against his former team in a dark patterned jacket and pants, while the rookie wore an all-white suit with a big chain.

Lions vs. Packers pregame notes

Detroit escaped the Bears by the skin of their teeth last week after building a big lead. The offense struggled to execute in the red zone in the second half, while the defense started to show some holes after another wave of critical injuries hit.

Detroit lost defensive linemen Josh Paschal (knee) and Levi Onwuzurike (hamstring) to injuries that left their statuses for the Green Bay game in the air and linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez for the season with a torn ACL. Running back Josh Jacobs has been the offensive hub, averaging 82.3 rushing yards per game, to open up the downfield passing attack for quarterback Jordan Love and a potent group of pass catchers led by former Michigan State standout Jayden Reed and tight end Tucker Kraft.

headline: U-M expands tuition-free program to students from families earning up to $125K
fullText:
More people will soon be able to attend the University of Michigan without paying tuition thanks to the Ann Arbor-based school expanding a program for current and future in-state students.

Starting in the fall, the university's "Go Blue Guarantee" will cover tuition for any student from a family with an annual income of $125,000 and assets of up to $125,000, according to a news release issued Thursday. That's a substantial increase from the previous $75,000 parameter.

“The Go Blue Guarantee breaks down economic barriers and ensures that a world-class education is available to Michigan students from all backgrounds, no matter their family’s economic means,” said U-M President Santa Ono in a statement.

New students and returning students who fall under the new income criterion are eligible. According to the program website, there is no separate application necessary to be considered for this financial aid at the Ann Arbor campus. New students at the Dearborn and Flint campuses are also eligible.

More: U-M researchers seek pancreatic cancer 'Holy Grail': An early detection test

More: Young leaders with Michigan connections make Forbes' 30 under 30 list: Who they are

Since launching the program in 2018, the university says it has covered the tuition of more than 8,000 students.

“As a state university, we have a responsibility to serve the people of Michigan and — given the many pressures of today’s economy — we want to ensure that working-class and middle-class Michiganders can send their children to this great university and benefit from all that it offers,” said Katherine White, chair of the Board of Regents, in a statement.

The expanded eligibility comes at a time when higher education costs continue to soar. The total cost to attend a four-year college — tuition, fees, room and board, etc. — increased more than 156% from 1963 to 2021, according to the National Center for Education Statistics.

This year, in-state students at the Ann Arbor campus pay about $17,700 for tuition. However, the university says 63% of in-state undergraduate students at the main campus receive grant or scholarship aid.

Expanding the program will cost the university about $8.8 million every year, the university stated.

headline: Mallie’s, the longtime downriver restaurant noted for gigantic burgers, shutters
fullText:
A downriver sports grill and bar noted for big offerings, including gigantic hamburgers, gallon-sized Bloody Marys, and two-pound tacos, has abruptly closed.

Mallie’s Sports Grill and Bar in Southgate, on the corner of Allen Road and Northline, shuttered after 19 years in business.

Its last day of operating, owner Steve Mallie told the Free Press, was the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, or what’s known as the busiest bar night of the year.

“It was the hardest decision I had to make,” Mallie said of closing the longtime bar and restaurant.

While Mallie said the place was running poorly and he was personally funding the restaurant, he’s also cited family reasons.

More: Alfred Talley, pioneering fast-food executive and longtime Southfield resident, dies at 94

More: Detroit, Michelin-starred, and James Beard-nominated chefs highlight chefs dinner series

“I am dealing with several family illnesses,” Mallie said. “It was hard for me to come up with this decision, but I have to take care of my family.”

The restaurant and bar operations are closed indefinitely. Mallie provided the Free Press with a screenshot of a post on the restaurant's employee Facebook page that read:

“This is terribly hard news for me to announce after over 19 years in business but due to recent circumstances and the decline health of my parents. I have decided to suspend the operations of the restaurant at this time.”

A Facebook post on the Downriver and Friends group was not kind to Mallie or the closing, especially before the holidays. While the post has since been taken down, it also mentioned unpaid Mallie’s bills and bounced employee paychecks.

Mallie acknowledged some bounced paychecks but told the Free Press he made good on them.

"The business was not making enough to support itself," Mallie said.

About 40 people were employed at the grill and bar, Mallie said, and the place is about four times the space as the Thirst Parlor in Wyandotte, which Mallie co-owns.

Thirst Parlor, a Prohibition-themed bar with a food menu, opened in 2022, and it remains open. Mallie said some employees have moved to the Thirst Parlor location.

More than a half-dozen years ago, Mallie and his staff set a record for building the largest cheeseburger commercially available, at nearly 1,800 pounds.

headline: Devin Booker reflects on Phoenix Suns' legend Walter Davis after scoring milestone
fullText:
Devin Booker only speaks in reverence about Walter Davis.

“Big Poppa. It’s Smooth Operator. A legend, rest in peace," Booker said after the Suns beat the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday.

Booker's brevity spoke volumes regarding his thoughts about the Phoenix Suns' all-time leading scorer and late Hall of Famer. Booker's first field goal against the Spurs matched Davis as the only two Suns players to ever reach 15,000 career points entirely scored in a Phoenix uniform.

The 10-year veteran Booker finished with 29 points, putting him at just 639 away from Davis's franchise record of 15,666.

Booker prides himself on being a historian. He's known to drive muscle cars, collect items and occasionally wear fashion relics from decades ago. So Booker's continued response about being influenced by one of the Phoenix Suns' earliest stars in Davis, and his impact on the city and the NBA sounded natural.

“Yeah, I’ve done my research, watched all the highlights, so to even be close to what he’s done for this franchise, it’s just a crazy situation to be in," Booker said. "But we have to continue to honor him, live through him, show appreciation for the ones that came before us and laid the groundwork for us."

Davis was inducted into the Naismith Hall of Fame in October. He was drafted by Phoenix out of North Carolina in 1977 and played the first 11 of his 15-year career in the Valley. Davis was a six-time All-Star during his tenure in Phoenix and averaged 20.6 points on 52% shooting.

Michael Jordan said during his 2009 Hall of Fame induction speech that he grew up as an "NC State guy" because of his childhood idol and fellow Hall of Famer David Thompson. But Jordan once cited Davis among his inspirations, and Jordan rose to fame at NC State's in-state rival UNC five years after Davis entered the league.

Davis's peers and fans nicknamed Davis "Sweet D" for his fluid jumpshot form and "The Greyhound" for his fast-paced transition scoring. Booker's and Davis's height and position as 6-6 shooting guards, offensive styles, and defensive intensity were similar.

Davis didn't attend the revamped Suns Ring of Honor ceremony on Oct. 29, 2023, where his No. 6 jersey was honored again in the Footprint Center rafters. Four days later, he passed away from natural causes at age 69 in Charlotte.

Booker spoke about his seldom interactions with Davis at former Suns owner Jerry Colangelo's annual Golf Classic in Phoenix, which draws numerous Hall of Famers.

“We would just talk in passing," Booker said. "Seen him at Colangelo’s event once before or two, but the respect is always there. I’ve always showed love to the legends. I always keep that a big part of everything I do in every aspect of life. I try to do it through my (Nike Book 1) shoes, just continue to tell stories because I’m a historian in a way. I understand how important it is for the people that laid the foundation for us.”

headline: GOP sues to block Proposition 479, the $15B countywide transportation measure
fullText:
The Maricopa County Republican Committee sued to challenge the passage of Proposition 479, which was approved by voters to raise billions of dollars for the Valley's highways, roads and bus routes.

Attorney Bryan Blehm filed the complaint Nov. 30 in Maricopa County Superior Court, asserting the ballot measure only garnered 59.82% of the vote and should not stand because voters amended the Arizona Constitution in 2022 to "require all tax measures to receive at least 60% of the votes cast."

Blehm argued the courts should decertify the results because they fell short of the 60% threshold established by the passage of Proposition 132. The lawsuit names the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors, which played a key role in certifying the results.

Blehm could not be immediately reached for comment.

Connect Maricopa, the campaign committee supporting Proposition 479, filed a motion to intervene on Wednesday, according to the Superior Court website. The Arizona Republic could not immediately reach a committee representative for comment.

Phoenix mayor: 'Lawsuit is deeply flawed and misguided'

Marty Shultz was a vocal advocate for the regional transportation tax and chairman of Proposition 479's original predecessor, Proposition 300, which Maricopa County voters approved in 1985. Voters extended the tax in 2004 when they passed Proposition 400. Last month, voters overwhelmingly agreed to extend funding again at the same tax rate that's been in place nearly 40 years.

Shultz said Blehm's central legal argument was faulty because the Proposition 132 burden only applies to constitutional amendments.

"Proposition 479 is a legitimate referral by The Arizona Legislature. It is not a constitutional amendment," Shultz said.

"Having been involved in politics for four or five decades, I’m not surprised by much, and I’m not surprised by this lawsuit brought about by the Arizona Republican Party and the minions that have an unreasonable conservative bent to their thinking," Shultz said, adding, "Hopefully this ill-conceived action will not subject 479 to any sanctions or reversal."

When lawmakers were debating this issue in 2023, they clarified that a constitutional amendment that requires 60% approval for any tax measure applies only to statewide issues. The transportation tax extension is a Maricopa County issue, not a statewide matter.

Officials at the Maricopa Association of Governments, a quasi-governmental agency that creates the regional transportation spending plan, could not immediately be reached for comment.

Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego reacted Wednesday, saying, “Maricopa County voters overwhelmingly passed Prop. 479 because they understand that a strong transportation system isn’t political. It's critical to our future. This lawsuit is deeply flawed and misguided, and I hope the courts recognize its malignant intentions.”

Proposition 479 asked voters to continue a half-cent sales tax for the next 20 years. Voters first approved it in 1985, then again in 2004. The tax provides revenue for the regional transportation plan approved by mayors across the Valley. The tax accounts for $14.9 billion of the $28.2 billion plan, so a little more than half.

It is set to fund freeways (40.5%), bus transit and bus rapid transit (33.5%), major roadways a regional transportation infrastructure (22.5%) and light rail maintenance (3.5%). But paired with other funding sources, it unlocks billions in federal funding that frees city revenue in Phoenix, Mesa and Tempe to expand the light rail 11.9 miles and the streetcar 4.4 miles.

Who filed the challenge to Proposition 479?

Blehm has a history of questionable election challenges.

He was issued a 60-day suspension by the state bar for lying while representing Republican Kari Lake in a lawsuit that sought to overturn the results of the 2022 gubernatorial election. The Arizona Supreme Court fined Blehm and another attorney $2,000 for making "unequivocally false" claims in that case.

He represented a conservative election-denial group in a legal battle with Maricopa County over public records earlier this year. He may not have been licensed to practice law during a trial in that case, because of a "fees-related issue," the county's lawyers said in open court at the time.

Shultz repeated the campaign argument that such an investment is vital to the region's economic development.

"Our economic success over the decades has been based, in part, on the development of a comprehensive transportation system," he said."What the perpetrators of this lawsuit failed to understand is that the economy, that they say they believe in, doesn’t just happen," Shultz said.

"I intend to call key Republican leaders and members of the Republican Party and 'complain like hell' over this behavior. It’s inappropriate, sends the wrong signal, and it probably will fail in court."

headline: Looking for chicken breast recipes? These are our favorite easy dinner ideas
fullText:
Chicken is inexpensive, easy to love, and can be made in seemingly endless ways, which is why it's a go-to protein for busy weeknight dinners.

The best part about these chicken dinners is that they come together quickly, many dirtying up only one pot or sheet pan, plus, they're very customizable and most ingredients are items you'll already have on hand. As long as you've got chicken in your fridge or freezer, you're more than halfway to a delicious dish.

If you need some inspiration, here are a few of our favorite recipes, from Americanized Chinese classics to Italian comfort food, cozy stews to sheet pan meals.

White chicken chili recipe

Store leftover chicken chili in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen chili overnight in the refrigerator before reheating in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Note that this white chicken chili thickens as it sits, so plan to add more broth (or water) when reheating.

Makes: 4 servings

Ingredients:

  • 2 (15-ounce) cans cannellini beans (white kidney beans), rinsed and drained
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 cup chopped yellow onion, about 1 small onion
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced or 2 teaspoons pre-minced garlic
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon chili powder
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • ½ teaspoon ground coriander
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • 4 cups chicken broth or stock
  • 2 (4-ounce) cans chopped or minced green chilies, undrained
  • 8 ounces cream cheese, cut into small pieces
  • 11-ounce can fiesta-style corn with peppers, drained (alternatively, 1 ¼ cups frozen corn, kept frozen until ready to use)
  • 4 cups shredded rotisserie chicken meat (about 1 rotisserie chicken), or any cooked chicken
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving

Optional for serving:

  • Flour or corn tortillas
  • Mexican cheese blend, Monterrey jack cheese, pepper jack cheese, queso fresco or cotija
  • Diced avocado
  • Chopped green onions
  • Fresh cilantro
  • Lime wedges

Instructions:

  1. Place half of the beans in a bowl and mash with a potato masher or fork until fully mashed. (The mashed beans act as a thickener, so the more they’re mashed, the better. You can also puree them in a food processor with a little of the broth.) Set aside.
  2. Heat the oil in a large saucepan or stock pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, chili powder, oregano, coriander, ½ teaspoon salt, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper and stir to combine. Cook for 1 minute, until the spices are fragrant.  
  3. Add the chicken broth, green chilies and reserved mashed beans and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium, partially cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
  4. Add the cream cheese, corn and remaining whole beans and return to a simmer. Simmer until the cream cheese melts and is incorporated.
  5. Stir in the chicken and tablespoon of lime juice and simmer for 5 minutes. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
  6. To serve, ladle the chili into bowls and finish with toppings like fresh cilantro, spring onions and cheese with tortillas and lime wedges on the side.

Orange chicken recipe

To round out your meal, I suggest serving orange chicken with fluffy jasmine rice or Asian noodles and steamed or roasted vegetables, such as broccoli, asparagus, snap peas, snow peas and green beans.

Makes: 4 servings

Ingredients:

For the chicken:

  • 2 large eggs
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • ½ cup cornstarch
  • ½ cup all-purpose flour
  • 1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts, tenders or thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
  • Oil for frying, such as vegetable oil, avocado oil, canola oil or peanut oil

For the orange glaze:

  • 1 cup orange juice
  • ¼ cup soy sauce, regular or low sodium
  • ¼ cup light or dark brown sugar
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • ½ teaspoon sesame oil
  • ½ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or more/less to taste
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ¼ teaspoon ground ginger
  • 2 tablespoons cornstarch
  • Chopped green onions for serving
  • Cooked jasmine rice or noodles for serving

Instructions:

  1. To prepare the chicken, in a shallow bowl, whisk together the eggs and season with salt and black pepper. 
  2. In another shallow bowl or dish, whisk together the cornstarch and flour.
  3. Dip the chicken in the eggs and turn to coat. Shake off excess egg, transfer the chicken to the cornstarch mixture, and turn to coat. Shake off excess cornstarch mixture.
  4. Heat about ¼-inch of oil in a high-sided skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 350 to 360 degrees F.
  5. Working in batches to prevent crowding the pan, add the chicken to the hot oil and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through, turning frequently. Using a slotted spoon or tongs, transfer the chicken to paper towels to drain.
  6. While the chicken is cooking, make the sauce. In a medium bowl or measuring cup, whisk together the orange juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, sesame oil, crushed red pepper flakes, garlic powder and ginger.  
  7. When all the chicken is finished cooking, wipe the oil from the pan and set the pan over medium-high heat. Add the sauce, bring to a simmer, and cook for 1 minute.
  8. In a small bowl, whisk together ½ cup cold water and 2 tablespoons of cornstarch. Add the mixture to the sauce and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
  9. Return the chicken to the pan and toss to coat with the sauce.
  10. Top the chicken with green onions and serve immediately atop jasmine rice or noodles.

Chicken and dumplings recipe

Store leftover chicken and dumplings in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating on the cooktop, adding more liquid as needed to loosen up the broth.

Makes: 4 servings

Ingredients:

For the soup:

  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons butter
  • 3 carrots, peeled and chopped
  • 2 stalks celery, chopped
  • 1 yellow onion, chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • ½ cup all-purpose flour
  • 5 cups chicken broth
  • 4 teaspoons chicken bouillon paste (such as Better Than Bouillon), or 2 chicken bouillon cubes
  • ½ teaspoon dried thyme
  • ¼ teaspoon dried sage
  • 2 bay leaves
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • 4 cups shredded cooked chicken, preferably rotisserie chicken meat
  • ½ cup heavy cream
  • ½ cup frozen peas kept frozen until ready to use
  • Chopped fresh parsley for serving

For the dumplings:

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 tablespoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup milk
  • 2 tablespoons melted butter

Instructions:

  1. Heat the oil and butter in a large saucepan or stock pot (whatever you use should have a lid) over medium-high heat.
  2. Add the carrots, celery and onion and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, or until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the flour and stir to coat. Cook for 1 minute.
  3. Add the broth, bouillon, thyme, sage, bay leaves, ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in the chicken, cream and peas and reduce the heat to low. Let the mixture simmer while you make the dumplings.
  4. To make the dumplings, in a medium bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the milk and melted butter and stir gently to combine, being careful not to overmix.
  5. If the soup isn’t simmering, increase the heat slightly so you have a gentle simmer; you don’t want boiling liquid, just a nice simmer. Using a medium cookie scoop (1 ½ tablespoons) or large spoon, drop the dumpling dough on top of the simmering liquid in a single layer.
  6. Cover the pan with a lid and simmer for 15 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted into a dumpling comes out clean. If the dumplings are still doughy, cover and continue cooking until finished.
  7. Remove from heat, ladle into bowls (removing bay leaves as you spot them), top with parsley and serve immediately.

Marry me chicken

You'll see this dish called creamy Tuscan chicken or marry me chicken. Whatever you call it, this recipe makes a decent amount of mouth-watering cream sauce, so be sure to serve it with something starchy so you don’t miss a drop. Great options include rice, polenta, mashed potatoes or mashed cauliflower, couscous, quinoa, bulger or other grains or egg noodles. A warm, crusty loaf of Italian bread would also be lovely. Store leftover chicken and sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three days or in the freezer for up to three months.

Makes: 4 servings

Ingredients:

  • 4 (5- to 6-ounce) boneless skinless chicken breasts
  • 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • 3 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • ⅓ cup finely chopped onion
  • ½ cup drained, oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, thinly sliced
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 packed cups baby spinach leaves
  • 1 ½ cups heavy cream
  • ¼ cup grated parmesan cheese, preferably freshly grated

Instructions:

  1. Season both sides of the chicken with the Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.
  2. Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large, non-reactive skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and sear until golden brown on both sides. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
  3. Heat the remaining tablespoon of oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, until soft. Add the sun-dried tomatoes and garlic and cook for 1 minute more, until fragrant.
  4. Add the spinach, and cook for 1 minute, just until the leaves just start to wilt.
  5. Add the heavy cream and parmesan cheese and bring to a simmer. Return the chicken to the pan with any accumulated juices from the plate. Simmer for 5 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens. Remove from heat and serve at once.

Sheet pan lemon rosemary chicken

This recipe is endlessly adaptable, so feel free to use what you have on hand. If you want to use bone-in thighs, increase the cooking time by about five to eight minutes.

Serves: 4

Ingredients:

  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for coating the potatoes and peppers
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1 ½ teaspoons fresh rosemary leaves or 1 teaspoon dried
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1-pound bone-in skinless chicken breasts (or 2 ½ pounds skinless chicken thighs)
  • 1 pound small red potatoes, scrubbed clean and halved
  • 2 bell peppers, any color, seeded, cut into 2-inch pieces, or 4-6 mini peppers, halved and seeded
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • Chopped fresh parsley for serving (optional)

Preparation:

  1. Preheat the oven to 400 F.
  2. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
  3. In a shallow dish or zip-top bag, combine the olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, rosemary and garlic. Add the chicken and turn to coat, working the marinade into the chicken with your hands. (At this point, you can refrigerate the chicken for up to 24 hours if you aren't ready to cook yet.)
  4. Arrange the chicken on the prepared pan in a single layer. Toss the potatoes with about 1 tablespoon of olive oil and arrange them around the chicken in a single layer. Season the chicken and potatoes with salt and black pepper. Bake for 20 minutes.
  5. Toss the bell peppers with a little olive oil.  Carefully remove the sheet pan and arrange the peppers alongside the chicken and potatoes. Return to oven and bake for 5 to 10 minutes more or until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through (a meat thermometer should register 165 degrees), the potatoes are tender and the peppers are slightly charred.
  6. Remove sheet pan from the oven and top the chicken and vegetables with fresh parsley (if using). Plate or serve directly from the sheet pan.
