headline: Yelp Best New Restaurants list has 2 Nashville spots; you might not have heard of No. 12
fullText:
Yelp, the site that helped make everyone a food critic regardless of credentials, has just released its Best New Restaurants of 2024, and two Nashville dining spots are on the list.

To arrive at the findings, the website's data team analyzed business ratings and review volume for restaurants that opened in the last year and a half. They also identified a few trends.

First, Japanese cuisine is hot. We've seen this in Nashville with the opening of omakase-style sushi restaurants, including Sushi | Bar and the forthcoming Kase by Noko.

Noko (701 Porter Road), East Nashville's wood-fired pan-Asian restaurant, landed in second place overall on Yelp's top 25, one of a half-dozen Japanese concepts on the list.

More: New Nashville restaurant offers first all-omakase experience. Here's what to expect

Noko's menu includes plenty of bright raw fish preparations and other Asian-influenced small plates, but the star of the restaurant is a wood-driven grill that fires pork ribs, roasted seasonal vegetables and a somewhat dramatically large tomahawk ribeye. The sleeper hit is the restaurant's brunch, where you can get karaage fried chicken rice bowls, poke and wood-grilled steak and eggs.

Another new Nashville restaurant nearly cracked the top 10: Gannons Nashville (170 Fourth Ave. N.), which came in at No. 12. That's the house eatery of the Marriott Courtyard near Printers Alley. It features the food of executive chef Gannon Leary, previously the chef at Skull’s Rainbow Room. That restaurant opened in the summer of 2023.

The menu at Gannons features oysters on the half-shell and Rockefeller-style and other old-school dishes from the glory days of hotel dining mixed with modern American offerings. You can find Caesar salad sharing the menu with empanadas, lamb racks and Louisiana-style barbecued shrimp.

If Yelp's analysis is correct, there's a good chance you'll be landing at one or both of Nashville's winning restaurants soon.

Yelp's research indicates that food-industry sales will reach $1 trillion this year, a first for the American dining scene.

And diners particularly love everything new and shiny; searches for “best new restaurants near me” increased 43% in the first three quarters of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023, Yelp researchers found.

headline: 'Search for Dolly': Dolly Parton announces casting call for Broadway musical. Can you play the Queen of Country Music?
fullText:
Think you have what it takes to depict the legendary Dolly Parton on stage? It could be your time to shine.

Parton herself has announced a national casting call for her upcoming Broadway musical, "Dolly: An Original Musical." The "Search For Dolly" officially kicked off on Thursday afternoon, seeking out talent across America for the 2026 musical.

"As you may have heard, my life story is coming to Broadway in a brand new show called 'Dolly: An Original Musical," Parton said in an announcement video. "And now, I'm announcing the search for Dolly ... I wanna give you the chance to help me bring my story to Broadway — and maybe even play me!"

“We're looking for talented performers who can capture the spirit of my journey, whether you're an experienced theater professional or an undiscovered gem with that little special something," Parton continued.

"So, what are you waiting for? This might be your moment to take center stage and step into the spotlight. Break a leg!” 

More Dolly: Dolly Parton surprises at CMA Fest with Nashville hotel, musical announcement and much, much more

After the video audition phase, a selected few will get the opportunity to audition in person in front of the show's casting director, Parton said.

The musical, which will be directed by Bartlett Sher ("The Light in the Piazza"), will feature both new and old tunes written by Dolly Parton.

Here's what to know about the nation-wide audition casting call.

More: Who will play Dolly Parton in her 'Hello, I'm Dolly' Broadway musical? Everything we know so far

Here's how to submit your audition for the Dolly Parton musical

In order to submit an audition, you need to record a video introducing yourself and singing one minute of your favorite Dolly Parton tune.

From there, you can upload the song to the social media platform of your choice, including Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, and tag #SearchForDolly.

Next, you need to fill out an application form at dollymusical.com.

When is the deadline to submit a Dolly Parton musical audition?

You can submit an audition video until Jan. 12, 2025.

What are the Dolly Parton musical submission requirements?

  • Submit a one minute performance of one of Parton's songs
  • Introduce yourself at the start of the video and share where you're from
  • List your name, location and contact information on the audition form on the musical's website
  • If you're under 18 years old, you must share your date of birth and acquire parental/guardian permission

To learn more about the musical and stay up to date, visit dollymusical.com.

headline: Carrie Underwood to headline ABC's country-heavy New Years Eve spectacular. How to watch
fullText:
Fresh from the Vegas stage and months before kicking off work on the latest season of American Idol, award-winning country superstar Carrie Underwood will hit ABC's stage for "Dick Clark's Rockin' New Year's Eve" in New York City's Times Square.

Carrie Underwood successfully closing 2024, opening 2025

headline: Tennessee Sen. Ken Yager, charged with DUI, must hold himself to higher standard | Opinion
fullText:
As a Tennessee lawmaker, state Sen. Ken Yager knows it is wrong − and illegal − to drive drunk and leave the scene of an accident.

That's why it was a hapless understatement when Kingston Republican told the press that he was involved in "an unfortunate incident" Tuesday. That incident involved a Georgia trooper arresting the 77-year-old lawmaker for driving under the influence and leaving the scene of an accident.

Yager is owed fairness under the law and he has not been convicted of any crime, but the video of his failed sobriety test is just painful to watch.

More important, as a public official, he is and must be held to a higher standard. Surely, he knows that too.

Sen. Yager has a responsibility to make things right after DUI arrest

This is an important time to remind all citizens that in the U.S., 37 people per day die in crashes involving drunk driving, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. In 2022, that amounted to 13,524 deaths − 364 in Tennessee and 507 in Georgia that year.

Tennessee law prohibits motorists from consuming or possessing an open container of alcohol, although that restriction does not apply to passengers.

It is encouraging to know that Yager said he is cooperating with authorities.

In the meantime, he should reflect on what further steps he might take to rectify the unfortunate accusations against him.

That may involve getting alcohol use disorder treatment. It should also involve being committed to public service announcements discouraging drunk and/or impaired driving.

He should consider working with Tennessee state officials and nonprofit on a video and/or billboard campaign to bring that message home. He could also sponsor legislation to close loopholes in open container laws for passengers.

Voters re-elected him in a landslide. That is not a license for recklessness

As for his own Senate seat, Yager must think long and hard if he is up to the challenge of fulfilling the public trust anymore.

In the Nov. 5 election, 85% of District 12 voters sent him back to the legislature. He won in a landslide, but this mandate does not permit him to flout the law.

His colleagues may also have second thoughts about Yager's position as chairman of the Senate Republican Caucus.

If he is indicted for the accusations against him, he should resign that leadership position and not seek to reclaim the post for the next legislative session.

At a time when politicians on both sides of the aisle nationally are questioning the fairness of the justice system, the Tennessee General Assembly has sent a message in its legislation that the Volunteer State is about being tough on crime and about law and order.

Yager has supported these measures, and if he honestly believes it, as this legal process unfolds, he should put the good of the public over his own political ambitions.

headline: Jared Curtis, Nashville Christian power past Columbia Academy to win Division II-A title
fullText:
For the third time in four seasons, Nashville Christian was back in the TSSAA football championship.

And for the second time in school history, the Eagles are Division II-A state champions.

Keyed by Jared Curtis' six total touchdowns, Nashville Christian ran away with the 49-21 win over Columbia Academy on Thursday in Chattanooga.

The game was tied at 14-14 at halftime, and Nashville Christian scored touchdowns on its first five second-half drives to run away with the victory.

Curtis finished 8-of-16 for 156 yards and two passing TDs along with 60 rushing yards and four scores. Terry Ward had a game-high 203 rushing yards, most of which came in the second half, along with a rushing TD.

Columbia Academy's offense moved the ball but struggled with finishing drives and turnovers. Montae Baldwin finished with 189 total yards (167 rushing, 22 receiving), while Harrison Brownlee scored all three touchdowns (one rushing, two receiving).

Recap the DII-A championship below:

TSSAA football championship game live updates: Nashville Christian vs. Columbia Academy in Division II-A game

Nashville Christian 42, Columbia Academy 21 with 4:09 left fourth quarter: Harrison Brownlee's third touchdown of the day

Columbia Academy is back on the scoreboard with a Harrison Brownlee 24-yard touchdown catch. PAT good. Nice throw by Stephen Nieves.

Nashville Christian recovers the onside kick.

Nashville Christian 42, Columbia Academy 14 with 5:19 left fourth quarter: Jared Curtis TD run No. 4

Nashville Christian recovers the kickoff after it drops short of a Columbia Academy player, and the Eagles cash in. Jared Curtis caps the drive with his fourth touchdown run on a 4-yard carry.

PAT good. Nashville Christian is rolling.

Nashville Christian 35, Columbia Academy 14 with 7:55 left fourth quarter: TJ Ward 64-yard TD run

Nashville Christian is cruising now. TJ Ward carries for a 64-yard touchdown run to all but put the game away. Ward is up to 177 rushing yards. PAT good.

Nashville Christian 28, Columbia Academy 14 with 11:13 left fourth quarter: Jared Curtis up to 3 TD runs

Jared Curtis caps another run-based Nashville Christian scoring drive with a 1-yard TD run. Two-point conversion is successful, with Curtis finding Zane Crampton for a completion.

TJ Ward is up to 113 rushing yards, including a 67-yard run to key the latest drive. Nashville Christian is closing in on a state title.

Nashville Christian 20, Columbia Academy 14 with 6:41 left third quarter: Jared Curtis' second TD run of the game

Nashville Christian orchestrates a touchdown drive to open the second half, capped by a Jared Curtis 3-yard touchdown run. PAT is no good.

If CA can stay in this game, Nashville Christian's kicking issues could be a major factor in the fourth quarter.

Jared Curtis stats in TSSAA football championships

Jared Curtis is 4-of-10 for 91 yards and a touchdown pass through one half, with a 6-yard touchdown run also to his credit. Columbia Academy has done a solid job defensively of making Curtis uncomfortable, but the 5-star QB has made a couple plays anyway.

HALFTIME: Nashville Christian 14, Columbia Academy 14

Columbia Academy gets the ball with 1:00 left in the second quarter and cash in. After a Wyatt Ayers 48-yard catch, CA scores with four seconds left on Harrison Brownlee's 11-yard touchdown catch from Stephen Nieves. PAT good.

All tied after one half in the DII-A championship game. CA is outgaining Nashville Christian 223-110.

Columbia Academy comes up empty after turnover

Nashville Christian loses a fumble on its first play after the Columbia Academy touchdown, and CA recovers. But the Bulldogs are forced to go for it on 4th and goal near the 10-yard line, and Stephen Nieves is intercepted by Blair Otero. Nashville Christian has three first-half takeaways, all interceptions.

Nashville Christian 14, Columbia Academy 7 with 5:53 left second quarter: Columbia Academy cuts into the lead

Harrison Brownlee plunges into the end zone from a yard out to get Columbia Academy on the board in the second quarter. PAT good. Nice response.

Montae Baldwin has 88 total yards already, including a key 22-yard reception on a fourth down play to set up the Columbia Academy score.

Nashville Christian 14, Columbia Academy 0 with 9:53 left second quarter: Jared Curtis to Javin Drewelow

Jared Curtis finds Javin Drewelow on a quick slant, and Drewelow makes one defender miss before winning the race to the pylon for a 35-yard touchdown catch.

On the two-point try, Curtis pitches to offensive lineman Pryor Browning lined up as an H-back, and Browning dives into the end zone for the successful try.

Nashville Christian 6, Columbia Academy 0 with 4:37 left first quarter: Jared Curtis TD run opens the scoring

After a Nashville Christian interception, the Eagles drive down the field via the ground game. Jared Curtis caps the drive with a 6-yard touchdown run. PAT no good.

Curtis was flagged for spinning the ball after the play. That's really a penalty, TSSAA?

headline: TripAdvisor just named this Nashville hotel as one of the best in the country for the second year in a row
fullText:
A Nashville hotel has been named among the best in the country by TripAdvisor for the second year in a row.

TripAdvisor named The Joseph, a Luxury Collection Hotel among the top 20 hotels in the country as part of its "Travelers’ Choice 2024 Awards Best of the Best" which celebrates the "highest level of excellence in travel."

The award is given to those who receive a high volume of stellar reviews and opinions from the TripAdvisor community over a 12-month period. According to TripAdvisor, fewer than 1% out of their 8 million listings achieve this milestone.

The Joseph, located near Broadway, came in at No. 19, behind hotels in Hawaii, North Carolina and Texas. At The Joseph, guests can enjoy spacious luxury suites, fine dining, a spa, salon, and a display of world-class art.

According to TripAdvisor, guests most love the pool, salon and rooftop bar.

"The Joseph's sophisticated design, meticulous craftsmanship, thoughtful service, and exceptional dining tell a story of Nashville at its most refined," said TripAdvisor.

headline: Tennessee State's Eddie George is runner-up for Eddie Robinson FCS Coach of the Year award
fullText:
Tennessee State football coach Eddie George was the runner-up for the 2024 Eddie Robinson FCS National Coach of the Year award presented by Stats Perform and announced Thursday.

Montana State coach was Brent Vigen won the award. His undefeated team is ranked No. 1 in the Stats Perform FCS Top 25 and set to play UT Martin Saturday in the second round of the national playoffs.

Vigen finished with 173 voting points while George finished with 115.

George, a former Tennessee Titans All-Pro running back in his fourth season at TSU, was the Big South/Ohio Valley Conference coach of the year after leading the Tigers to a 9-4 record and the national playoffs for the first time in 11 seasons and the seventh time in program history. TSU lost to Montana 41-27 last Saturday.

TSU also shared the Big South/OVC regular season championship marking only the third time the Tigers have won or shared the title. TSU won seven of its last eight regular season games and finished ranked No. 19 in the FCS Coaches poll and No. 21 in the Stats Perform poll.

George led the Tigers to back-to-back winning seasons for the first time in seven seasons and the third time in 25 seasons.

headline: Kentucky football's Barion Brown enters transfer portal after three seasons
fullText:
Former Pearl-Cohn star and 2021 Class 4A Mr. Football award winner Barion Brown will enter the transfer portal after three seasons with Kentucky football, he announced on social media Thursday.

"After much thought, prayer and conservations with my family, I have decided to enter the transfer portal for my final year of eligibility," Brown wrote in a graphic posted to Instagram. "Thank you for everything Big Blue Nation."

Brown, a junior, was a dynamic receiver and record-breaking returner in his Kentucky career, setting school and SEC records with five career kickoff return touchdowns, including three in 2023. For his efforts, he was named First Team All-America in 2023 as a returner by Sporting News. He recorded rushing, receiving and kickoff return touchdowns in Kentucky's loss to Clemson in the 2023 Gator Bowl.

But Brown's receiving numbers sagged from 628 yards to 539 yards as a sophomore and down to 361 yards as a junior as Kentucky's offense struggled in the post-Will Levis era. He still had his moments in 2024; Brown's 63-yard catch in the fourth quarter set Kentucky up for a go-ahead touchdown in the Wildcats' lone SEC win of the season over No. 6 Ole Miss. He finished the 2024 season with 361 receiving yards on 29 catches and three touchdowns while adding a rushing and kick return touchdown.

Brown signed with Kentucky in 2022 after a high school career as a football and track star at Pearl-Cohn.

Brown should garner interest from other Power conference programs given his speed, return ability and potential as a receiver.

headline: Suspect arrested after dozens of gunshots fired at Tennessee Pastor Greg Locke's home
fullText:
Police have arrested a suspect in connection to dozens of gunshots reportedly fired at Global Vision Bible Church Pastor Greg Locke's home, garage and vehicle at the time late night on Sept. 3 in western Wilson County.

Tyler Poole, 20, of Hermitage, is charged with aggravated assault, four counts of reckless endangerment with a deadly weapon, and two counts of vandalism, all stemming from the shooting in the 1700 block of Chandler Road, according to the Wilson County Sheriff's Office.

Poole is being held at the Wilson County Jail on a $50,000 bond, police stated on Wednesday.

There were no injuries reported at the time of the shooting.

Deputies responded to Locke's residence at the time near the former Global Vision Bible Church campus on Old Lebanon Dirt Road around 10:30 p.m. the night of the shooting and reported finding 30-40 shell casings around the house, garage and vehicle.

Global Vision recently moved from the property at 2060 Old Lebanon Dirt Road to 1010 Maddox Simpson Parkway in Lebanon. The first service in Lebanon was held Dec. 1.

Locke posted on social media just after the shooting in September that security footage showed a person "unloaded an entire magazine of bullets from an automatic weapon into our house, garage and my truck."Locke said "we" pulled into the driveway one minute after the shooting occurred, and one person was at the home.

One bullet cut through the headboard of the pastor's youngest daughter’s bed and lodged in her pillow, Locke posted on social media.

The pastor has gained a large social media following for his conservative political stances and the launch of a mass-deliverance ministry that involves casting out evil spirits. The church has also been known for events such as inviting people to burn items the church relates to witchcraft and the occult.

The investigation is continuing with the Wilson County Sheriff's Office working with other agencies.

headline: How Arnett Hayes described his record-setting game in BGA's TSSAA football championship loss
fullText:
CHATTANOOGA ― Arnett Hayes would have loved for the end of the TSSAA football playoffs to be different. He'd even sacrifice his historic production for a BGA win.

But that wasn't in the cards for the Wildcats, whose fourth-quarter rally attempt fell short in a 38-26 loss to CPA in the Division II-AA BlueCross Bowl state championship game Thursday at Finley Stadium.

Yet Hayes' fourth quarter was a memorable one for the BGA senior who set a state championship record for receiving yards, catching 15 passes for 260 yards and a touchdown. Hayes broke the previous record held by Giles County's Zach Bailey, who had 212 yards receiving against Greeneville in the Class 4A title game in 2009.

"I wasn't even thinking about how many catches and how many yards I had," Hayes said. "I was just thinking about trying to win a state championship. I mean, setting a state record is special but I'd rather have the win."

The Wildcats star gave CPA headaches. His 15 receptions were one shy of tying a state championship record for most receptions, held by USJ's Lee Mayhall, who had 16 against St. George's in the DII-A title game in 2011.

"That's our offense," BGA coach Bobby Bentley said. "We want to get our best players the ball in space and Arnett is great at that. Kaedyn (Marable) has done a great job of delivering the ball all year and Arnett has made play after play this season."

It was the first state championship appearance for BGA since 2018. It's been 21 years since the Wildcats won a title.

"We just couldn't stop (CPA's) run game," said Bentley, whose team surrendered 347 yards rushing to CPA, including 336 yards by the Lions' Rawls Patterson. "That's what we work on in the offseason. We've got to stop the run."

Hayes came into Thursday's championship game with 81 receptions for 1,113 yards and 13 TDs. He was the favorite target for Marable, a DII-AA Mr. Football finalist. Marable was 26-of-40 for 323 yards and two TDs, but his chemistry with Hayes this season was a big reason for BGA's 11-3 record.

He's the youngest of five kids that includes four sisters, Anastasia, Aislynn, Alasia and Acacia. His sisters played basketball at Riverdale while Anastasia, Aislynn and Alasia captured TSSAA basketball titles. 

"I knew I had to take that next step this year and this (championship) game was by far the most fun I've ever had in a game," Hayes said. "It was the biggest game I've ever played in, and, I mean, we lost and I'd rather win, but to have a game like this, it was something I'll never forget. And BGA will be back."

headline: How Rawls Patterson's career-best 336 rushing yards led CPA to TSSAA football championship
fullText:
CHATTANOOGA – Rawls Patterson picked the biggest game of the TSSAA football playoffs to have the best game of his career.

Patterson was unstoppable in the TSSAA football championships' Division II-AA game, leading CPA past BGA, 38-26. Patterson had 336 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 27 carries.

His 336 yards were the third most rushing yards in BlueCross Bowl history, behind Trezevant’s Cordarrian Richardson (342 yards in 2015) and Beech’s Jalen Hurd (394 yards in 2012). It was also the most yards and touchdowns Patterson has had in any game in his career.

More: TSSAA football championship game scores, live updates: Nashville Christian vs Columbia Academy in Division II-A

"There was one point in the game I looked up and it said 245 (yards), which is the most I've ever had, so just (at that point) I was like, 'Alright, I'm having a pretty good day,' " Patterson said. "I racked up a few more after that so it's just a beautiful day to be out here and ... it was awesome to come out with the win."

Patterson has been limited in touches during the season because of numerous lopsided games where he wasn't needed. When he's been able to get his touches, he's been one of the Nashville area's top ball carriers. But BGA saw very little of him in the two teams' regular-season meeting. Patterson was injured early in the game.

More: How Arnett Hayes described his record-setting game in BGA's TSSAA football championship loss

Patterson, the younger brother of former CPA stars Kane and Langston Patterson, was named the DII-AA BlueCross Bowl MVP after the game.

“It’s awesome because everybody’s goal was to be here, holding up the trophy after,” Patterson said. "I think more important than the trophy though are the relationships I've built. I think all the stats today, it's awesome to have that under your name but honestly I'm not doing any of that without the front five in front of me."

headline: McCallie completes 21-point comeback to stun rival Baylor, win Division II-AAA title
fullText:
McCallie staged a historic comeback to beat its biggest rival for a TSSAA football championship.

The Blue Tornado stormed back from a 21-0 deficit to win 27-21 over Baylor in the Division II-AAA state championship game on Thursday in Chattanooga.

McCallie running back Keylan Syam scored on a 2-yard touchdown run with 15 seconds left as the Blue Tornado took the lead for the first time in the game. The score capped a 98-yard drive over 5:25, and it was Syam's third touchdown run of the game.

Baylor took a 21-0 lead early in the second quarter after a Jamyan Theodore 69-yard touchdown catch, but the Red Raiders offense was stymied the rest of the game by the Blue Tornado defense.

McCallie changed the entire vibe of the game with Keeyshawn Tabuteau's 7-yard touchdown catch on the final play of the first half, cutting Baylor's lead to 21-6 at the break.

After trading possessions to open the third quarter, McCallie grinded out back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a pair of Syam 1-yard touchdown runs.

McCallie kicker Elliott Arnold missed a 27-yard go-ahead field goal attempt midway through the fourth quarter. But the Blue Tornado got a stop to get the ball back and set up the late dramatics.

Syam finished with 175 rushing yards on 34 carries. McCallie QB Elliott Drapeau was 18-of-31 for 237 yards and a touchdown with an interception. Drapeau made several key completions to move the chains on the final drive before the running game finished the deal.

Baylor RB David Gabriel Georges had 119 yards on 10 carries with a touchdown but left the game early in the fourth quarter with an undisclosed injury and did not return.

Recap the Division II-AAA championship below:

TSSAA football championship game live updates: Baylor vs. McCallie in Division II-AAA game

FINAL: McCallie completes comeback to win Division II-AAA title

Baylor's attempt to pitch the ball around turns into a fumble, recovered by McCallie. What a comeback by the Blue Tornado.

Final score: McCallie 27, Baylor 21. McCallie defends its Division II-AAA state championship.

Going to be a lot of people stunned not only by Baylor losing a game, but especially one in which it had a 21-0 lead.

McCallie takes the lead on a 98-yard drive

McCallie takes the lead with 15 seconds left on Keylan Syam's third touchdown run of the day to cap a 15-play, 98-yard drive in 5:25. What a drive and what a second half by the Blue Tornado.

Two-point try is good on an Elliott Drapeau carry. The McCallie QB made several key passes on the drive, including three straight completions to move the chains into Baylor territory.

McCallie 27, Baylor 21 with 15 seconds left.

McCallie converts on 4th and 2 from its own 10

Keylan Syam rushes around the left end on 4th and 2 for a 9-yard gain, so McCallie's drive continues. What a gutsy call from the Blue Tornado 10-yard line. If McCallie doesn't convert, Baylor has a prime chance to put the game away.

McCallie gets the ball on its own 2-yard line after Baylor punt

Baylor was lined up to go for it on 4th and 1 in McCallie territory, but a false start penalty changed the equation. Sam Shutters' 45-yard punt was downed at the McCallie 2-yard line, so a long way to go for the Blue Tornado with 5:40 remaining.

McCallie misses 27-yard go-ahead field goal attempt

McCallie kicker Elliott Arnold hooks a 27-yard field goal attempt wide left, and Baylor has an opportunity to re-take the momentum in this game. Still 7:46 to play in regulation. Baylor leads 21-19.

Arnold has been one of the state's best kickers, making 15-of-17 field goal attempts with a long of 51 per MaxPreps.

The Blue Tornado opted for the field goal try on 4th and 1 from the Baylor 10-yard line.

David Gabriel Georges injured in fourth quarter, out for rest of the game

Baylor running back David Gabriel Georges is helped off the field after an awkward tackle in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Georges had 119 rushing yards and a touchdown on 10 carries before leaving the game.

The TSSAA television broadcast reports Georges has been ruled out for the rest of the game. It appeared that Georges' ankle was being re-taped when he made it to the sideline.

McCallie's defense forces a 3-and-out and gets the ball in Baylor territory.

Baylor 21, McCallie 19 with 10:59 left fourth quarter: Blue Tornado score TD, miss out on two-point conversion

McCallie claws closer, with a 7-play, 75-yard drive capped by a Keylan Syam 1-yard touchdown run. The two-point conversion attempt is no good, with Elliott Drapeau tackled short of the goal line.

Plenty of time left, and this is going to be fun fourth quarter.

Baylor 21, McCallie 13 with 7:25 left third quarter: Blue Tornado cut Baylor's lead to one score

McCallie fumbles the ball near midfield on the opening drive of the second half, but forces a stop to get it back. Carson Lawrence's 44-yard catch sets up a Keylan Syam 1-yard touchdown run. PAT good.

Baylor's offense has been big play or bust so far tonight. It could use another big play coming up.

Halftime: Baylor 21, McCallie 6

McCallie gets on the board as time expires in the first half via a Keeyshawn Tabuteau 7-yard touchdown catch. PAT blocked.

The Blue Tornado get the ball to start the second half, so there's a path toward a competitive second half. Critical score to end the half.

Baylor 21, McCallie 0 with 9:44 left second quarter: Baylor's big-play offense strikes again

On 3rd and 10 from its own 31, Baylor and its big-play offense strikes again. Briggs Cherry hits a wide open Jamyan Theodore for a 69-yard touchdown pass. PAT good.

Baylor has scored touchdowns in three straight drives.

Baylor 14, McCallie 0 with 1:09 left first quarter: Joakim Dodson 43-yard TD catch

Baylor QB Briggs Cherry hits Tennessee signee Joakim Dodson in stride on a deep post for a 43-yard touchdown pass. PAT good.

McCallie's defense is having a lot of trouble keeping up with Baylor's skill players in the secondary. Been a couple defensive penalties on the McCallie secondary, plus the Dotson TD allowed.

Baylor 7, McCallie 0 with 5:19 left first quarter: David Gabriel-Georges 31-yard TD run

David Gabriel Georges may be the best running back in the state. He rips off a 31-yard touchdown run running through the left side to get Baylor on the board. PAT good.

Gabriel-Georges missed Baylor's first two playoff games with an injury, but he looks healthy tonight.

headline: Nashville Predators shut out 3-0 by Montreal Canadiens, lose sixth straight game
fullText:
The Nashville Predators now have six straight losses after falling 3-0 to the Montreal Canadiens on Thursday at the Bell Centre.  

Goaltender Sam Montembeault stopped all 29 shots faced for his eighth win and third shutout of the season. Jake Evans, Patrik Laine, and Joel Armia each scored for the Canadiens.

Like Wednesday night's loss in Toronto, the Predators were unable to generate any offense at 5-on-5, but the main issues came on special teams. Nashville finished 0-for-6 on the power play, while allowing one power play goal and one shorthanded goal.

Justus Annunen made 27 saves in his debut for the Predators.

Nashville (7-14-6) face the Ottawa Senators on Saturday, while Montreal (10-13-3) hosts the Washington Capitals on Saturday.

Montreal Canadiens lead Nashville Predators 1-0 on shorthanded goal

At the 6:58 mark of the first period, the Canadiens took the first penalty of the game, a bench minor for having too many men on the ice.

Less than a minute later, the Canadiens also scored the first goal of the game, a shorthanded goal from Jake Evans.

Pressure from the Montreal penalty killers forced a 2-on-1 in the Nashville zone and Evans was able to rip a shot by Predators' goaltender Justus Annunen.

Nashville Predators' Ryan O'Reilly out week to week with lower body injury

The Predators have been relatively healthy this season, but suddenly that's starting to change.

On Thursday before puck drop with the Canadiens, the Predators announced that Ryan O'Reilly is out week to week with a lower body injury. In addition, Jeremy Lauzon has been place on injured reserve as he continues to battle a lower body injury.

Though Michael McCarron will return for the first time since Nov. 20, the Predators' already weak center depth is now worse without O'Reilly. According to the official starting lineup, Steven Stamkos will begin as the team's top center, followed by Fedor Svechkov, Juuso Parssinen, and McCarron.

headline: Tennessee books bans are political theater. Protect kids with food and safety. | Opinion
fullText:
Over the last several months, a vocal group – often affiliated with local churches – has campaigned to remove books from Rutherford County school libraries.

They claim these books harm children by exposing them to explicit content, arguing that banning them is necessary to protect young minds and reflect their biblical worldview. However, these efforts have diverted attention and energy from solutions that would genuinely improve the lives of children and families in our community.

Banning books in the name of “protecting children” because they contain ideas or content deemed inappropriate doesn’t shield kids – it sets them up to be ill-prepared for adulthood.

Denying access to diverse perspectives, historical truths, and inclusive representation undermines children’s education and critical thinking skills. Instead of focusing on performative actions like book bans, we should direct our energy toward policies that address real challenges and provide meaningful support for families.

Give students food, don’t take away their reading materials

One tangible way to protect and support children is ensuring every student in Rutherford County schools has access to free breakfast and lunch.

Nearly 46% of households in the county struggle to keep up with the cost of living. Providing universal free meals would not only improve students’ academic performance but also offer much-needed relief to local families.

Preventing any child from going hungry is a moral obligation that demands real action, not theatrical distractions.

The ongoing review and removal of books waste precious resources that our already underfunded public schools cannot afford to lose. Instead of spending time and effort on pulling books off shelves, we should focus on fully funding our schools to meet students’ actual needs.

Smaller class sizes, expanded mental health resources, and investments in quality, diverse curricula would empower students to thrive.

News story: Just before Banned Books Week, a Tennessee county voted to remove Toni Morrison's 'Beloved' and 5 other books from schools

Depriving them of books that teach empathy and understanding only limits their potential to grow into compassionate, well-rounded adults.

Firearms are a bigger threat to children than ideas in a book

If protecting children is truly the goal, why isn’t this same vocal group advocating for measures to address the leading cause of death for children in Tennessee: firearms?

Since 2018, firearms have been the No. 1 underlying cause of death in the state. Simple, common-sense solutions – such as extreme risk protection orders, universal background checks, and safe storage laws – would save lives. Yet instead of addressing this urgent crisis, the focus remains on banning books, an action that does nothing to protect kids from real harm.

The campaign to ban books is a loud, performative distraction from the real issues plaguing our community. Arguing that school libraries are filled with “pornography” diverts attention from solutions that would make a tangible difference in children’s lives. When nearly half of families in Rutherford County are struggling to make ends meet, when public schools lack the resources they need, and when gun violence remains an ongoing threat, we cannot afford to waste energy on divisive debates that harm more than they help.

It’s time to stop allowing distractions like book bans to dominate our conversations about protecting children. These debates, rooted in fear and division, do nothing to address the real challenges kids face every day – hunger, unsafe schools, underfunded classrooms, and the absence of mental health resources. Instead of restricting access to ideas and stories that foster empathy and understanding, let’s turn our focus to solutions that genuinely safeguard and uplift children.

As Jesus reminds us in Matthew 25:40: “Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.”

Let us honor this teaching by dedicating our energy to feeding the hungry, fully funding public schools, enacting common-sense policies that ensure safety, and building a community where every child can thrive. Protecting children isn’t about censorship – it’s about taking action to meet their real and urgent needs.

Matt Fee is a resident of Rutherford County and serves on the board of the Rutherford County Library Alliance and the Rutherford Neighborhood Alliance. He is also a former executive committee member of the Rutherford County Democratic Party and served as campaign manager for Tiffany Fee for School Board.

headline: CPA won another TSSAA football championship in DII-AA. Can it keep winning in DII-AAA?
fullText:
CHATTANOOGA – A few Christ Presbyterian Academy players could hardly wait for the TSSAA football state championship gold ball trophy to be handed to them. 

They had to restrain themselves several times before the Lions finally mobbed and screamed over the BlueCross Bowl trophy following a 38-26 win over Battle Ground Academy in the Division II-AA final Thursday at Finley Stadium. 

CPA senior quarterback Hutson Chance is used to seeing this from his school. He was in fifth grade the last time the Lions failed to reach a TSSAA football playoffs state final. 

“Being here often is awesome,” said Chance, a Tennessee baseball commitment. “At the beginning of the year, that’s always the goal, to wear the white championship hat.”

More: TSSAA football championship scores, live updates: Nashville Christian leads Columbia Academy after Jared Curtis TD

Now, can CPA keep putting on those hats?

The Lions (14-0) have been a model of consistency — winning their second straight state title and fourth in seven years — but their dominant DII-AA run has come to a close. The TSSAA moved CPA up to DII-AAA beginning in 2025, using a success factor tool in order to give DII-AAA 12 teams. The Lions leave DII-AA on a 26-game win streak.

CPA coach Ingle Martin is unhappy about the move. He wants TSSAA private schools to have an open discussion about how they can classify themselves more equally, with a focus on how much financial aid each school distributes. 

For now, Martin must prepare the Lions for their new world in DII-AAA — where Chattanooga boarding schools McCallie and Baylor have combined for every state title in that classification since it was formed before the 2020 season.  

Martin believes DII-AAA has become increasingly professionalized and that people are turning a blind eye to it.

More: Why TSSAA football teams can't use electronic helmet communication devices similar to NFL

“Do we want high school football in Tennessee to be the NCAA?” Martin said. “Because we’re headed there, and Division II-AAA is the closest thing to the NCAA that you can get to.” 

CPA has been the dominant figure in DII-AA for more than a decade. The Lions are 162-34 since 2011. 

More: How Arnett Hayes described his record-setting game in BGA's TSSAA football championship loss

More: How Rawls Patterson's career-best 336 rushing yards led CPA to TSSAA football championship

The Lions' success under Martin — five state championships and seven consecutive state final appearances — is helped by a strong developmental youth program and first-class strength and conditioning. The Lions have withstood losses from talented senior classes with players behind them who are physically capable of winning right away.  

Within that are generations of CPA families who’ve won titles together. CPA junior running back Rawls Patterson rushed for 336 yards and four touchdowns on 27 carries against BGA (11-3). Patterson's older brothers, Langston and Kane, both won state titles under Martin. 

Chance believes CPA can use the same winning formula in DII-AAA. 

“I wouldn’t change much. I really do think they can hang,” Chance said. “I’m excited to see what it’ll be like watching from afar.”

headline: Jelly Roll and Tennessee Titans visit juvenile offenders
fullText:
Good morning, friends, Tennessean columnist Brad Schmitt here. Y'all, I'm freezing my face off here this week! 🥶

Here's some feel-good news that'll surely warm you up.

'I want 'em to know they're loved'

Back in August, rapper/singer Jelly Roll — a famous arena-filling act from Antioch, y'all! — made a surprise visit to a Tennessee Titans team meeting.

Jelly Roll told 'em he'd been a fan since the Titans first played in Tennessee when his dad took him to a game in Memphis in the late '90s. Then, a year or two later, when Jelly Roll got locked up in juvenile detention, he watched the 2000 Music City Miracle on the Titans' stadium Jumbotron, which he could see from his cell.

Jelly Roll finished his six-minute talk that day with a unique invitation.

"That juvenile [facility] right there next to y’all’s stadium, I would love to host a few of y’all to come and talk to the kids and spread a little love," the rapper said. "Those kids need it.

"The Tennessee Titans stadium and juvenile have been connected the entire time the Titans stadium has been here. And I want to be the first guy that actually brings them together."

As Jelly Roll tells it, defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons practically chased down the rapper when his talk ended to ask when he and some of the other players could visit juvie.

That happened the Tuesday before Thanksgiving.

'I watched these kids turn into kids today'

On Nov. 24, Jelly Roll and Titans QB Will Levis, Jeffery Simmons, wide receivers Calvin Ridley and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, defensive lineman T’Vondre Sweat, offensive linemen JC Latham and Peter Skoronski, linebacker Arden Key, punter Ryan Stonehouse, head coach Brian Callahan, GM Ran Carthon and Titans President/CEO Burke Nihill went to Nashville's juvenile detention center.

And this was no quick meet-and-greet: Those guys spent three hours with about 50 kids in the pre-trial housing pod.

"I watched these kids turn into kids today," Jelly Roll said. "Normally they’re inmates, normally they’re convicts. I watched them let their guard down today. It was cool.

"I hope that this gives kids hope and a second chance, man, and I want ‘em to know they’re loved."

Check out some video highlights here.

Juvenile court officials were thrilled with the visits.

“An event like this, where the Titans — our neighbors — show they care, is truly special," said Anthony "Tony" Smith, spokesman and community outreach supervisor. "I see these kids every day, and it’s not often under joyful circumstances. Seeing them smile ear-to-ear today has been nothing short of amazing.”

Juvenile Court Judge Sheila Calloway said it's impossible to measure the benefits of the visit.

"For these young people, seeing role models like the Titans and Jelly Roll take time out of their busy schedules to sit with them, share a meal, and speak words of encouragement can be life changing," the judge told me. "It shows them that there are people who believe in their potential and want to see them succeed."

50,000th tree planted — and that's a lot of green

There's a public/private group called Root Nashville that decided six years ago to plant 500,000 trees in Nashville by 2050. That's an average of about 15,600 trees a year.

Well, this week, the group reached 10% of its goal. The 50,000th tree got planted at the entrance of 62-acre Whitsett Park in southeast Nashville. A bunch of elected officials and organization leaders were on hand with shovels and speeches.

Now if you're any good at math (unlike me), you might see that Root Nashville is a bit behind on reaching that half-a-million-tree-planted goal. So you can pitch in! And Root Nashville even will give you free trees to plant. Just go the website, rootnashville.org, to get started.

Thanks for spending another week with The Good News with Brad Schmitt. Your friends can sign up for this weekly emailed newsletter at tennessean.com/goodnews.

Please share those good news stories with me! I'm at brad@tennessean.com. Dig into more feel-good stories below.

headline: Avoid holiday donation Scrooges by following Tennessee Secretary of State's tips | Opinion
fullText:
In the holiday classic, “A Christmas Carol,” the main character − Ebenezer Scrooge − was a miser who hated Christmas. A visit from three spirits, the Ghost of Christmas Past, the Ghost of Christmas Present, and the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come led to Scrooge’s rebirth on Christmas morning, transforming him into a kinder, gentler man.

Unlike Scrooge, Tennesseans don’t need a visit from three spirits to remind them about the true meaning of the season.

National data suggests we are some of the most generous givers to charitable causes in the nation. This distinction comes with a warning − beware of those with bad intentions who would rather operate like cold-hearted misers, exploiting the goodwill and generosity of others.

Pay close attention to the charities to which you donate

Our office strives to help identify these Scrooges through a series of wise giving tips. The goal is to inform and educate consumers to ensure those deciding to give to one of the more than 11,000 active charitable organizations in Tennessee can have the greatest impact with their donation.

Tennesseans should do their research and ensure an entity is registered with the state through our website: https://sos.tn.gov/charities.

They should also say “Bah Humbug!”  to anyone pressuring them to give on the spot, ask questions about an organization’s mission, and determine who might benefit from a donation, and how much of their gift will support an individual or cause.

If you donate through an app or website, make sure all personal information provided as part of the process goes directly to the organization receiving your donation.

Opinion: Tennessee voters should avoid disinformation and rely on trusted information

Ask whether your contribution is tax-deductible and consider using a check or credit card for record-keeping purposes, instead of giving cash.

Lastly, pay close attention to the name of a nonprofit organization. Sometimes these entities have similar names, but that doesn’t mean they are associates − like Jacob Marley and Scrooge.

Tennessee can investigate and pursue violations of the law

Remember, the Division of Business and Charitable Organizations has the authority to investigate and impose civil penalties against groups that violate the Tennessee Charitable Solicitations Act.

If you have questions or concerns, or you think an entity is not operating in good faith, contact us at 615-741-2555.

Through these wise giving tips, you can treat every day like Christmas morning, give generously, and have a life-changing impact on a neighbor in need through your favorite charitable organization.

From all of us in the Tennessee Secretary of State’s office, we wish you a joyful holiday season, and to quote the most famous line from “A Christmas Carol” and the character Tiny Tim, “God bless us, everyone!”

Tre Hargett was elected by the Tennessee General Assembly to serve as the 37th secretary of state in 2009; he has been re-elected to this position in 2013, 2017, and 2021.

headline: Music-centric gift ideas for the country fan on your list
fullText:
Welcome to The Pick, The Tennessean music staff's weekly email conversation about all things you need to know — hot insider takes from Music City's legendary creative community, plus the who, what and where impacting our communities from Lower Broadway to Leiper's Fork and beyond.

Scott's "Yellow Rose" line is her most popular and is inspired by idyllic yellow Texas roses and the "vibrant joy" that the "tranquility and adventure" of Western culture.

Song You Need To Hear

Sister Sadie - “Make Me Stay or Make Me Go” - Multi-generational, all-female, Grammy and three-time International Bluegrass Music Association Vocal Group of the Year-winning sextet (with 2024 IBMA vocalist of the year Jaelee Roberts in the group) Sister Sadie have released a stellar folk-rock adjacent bluegrass love song. The music has a style and groove that feels solidly rooted in style without definition and space without time. Look no further if you are looking for a "new-old group" to claim as a "push play and stream the catalog all day" while preparing a holiday meal or house cleaning. What Roberts, Deanie Richardson, Gena Britt, Dani Flowers and Maddie Dalton are up to is nestled in an authentic, accessible groove.

headline: Lt. Gov. Randy McNally offers prayers for Yager; no GOP calls for senator to step down
fullText:
Tennessee Senate Republicans are not yet weighing in on whether Sen. Ken Yager should step down from his position as Republican Caucus chair, two days after he was arrested and charged in a hit-and-run crash and DUI while on vacation in Georgia.

Yager, R-Kingston, has called the event “an unfortunate incident,” but declined to comment on advice of his attorney. He is cooperating with Georgia authorities. 

Lt. Gov. Randy McNally, R-Oak Ridge, and Senate Speaker Pro Tempore Ferrell Haile, R-Gallatin, have declined to respond to questions on whether Yager should resign or step down from his position as Republican caucus chair.

“It is my understanding that Senator Yager is cooperating fully with the authorities in Georgia in this matter,” McNally said in a statement Thursday. “My thoughts and prayers are with he and his family as he does so.”

Yager was stopped by Georgia state troopers in Jekyll Island on Tuesday, after authorities were on the lookout for a Ford Edge involved in a hit-and-run. Troopers noticed a “distinct odor of alcohol on his breath,” according to the incident report, and Yager admitted he had been in a crash earlier after drinking “a couple glasses of wine previously in the day.”

During the stop, Yager repeatedly urinated on himself, and failed his field sobriety tests, which were cut short due to safety concerns while he was performing a one-leg stand, according to the report. A breathalyzer returned a breath alcohol content of 0.14, and he declined a blood test.

Yager was booked at the jail Tuesday evening, and released around 2 a.m. local time Wednesday. He has been charged with a hit and run, failure to stop at a stop sign, and driving under the influence.

If Yager is indicted, Senate ethics rules require Yager to step down as caucus chair, or appeal to the Ethics Committee for a hearing on whether or not he can keep the position.

The Senate Republican Caucus has not made a statement on the matter. 

The caucus stood by McNally last year after he drew national criticism over a string of interactions on social media with a scantily clad gay man, after backing a series of bills that LGBTQ advocates deemed discriminatory. Activists called on him to resign from his leadership post. McNally stepped away from social media at the time and was recently reelected as speaker of the Senate by the caucus.

Yager regularly pays lease expenses for a Ford with campaign funds. According to disclosures, Yager has spent $22,888 on the vehicle lease, car insurance, oil and tire maintenance, car washes, details and county vehicle registration fees since November 2022, with $16,615 going to his lease with Jerry Duncan Ford in Harriman. Before that, he paid vehicle lease expenses to a Lincoln dealership.

headline: Purdue football defensive leader Dillon Thieneman exploring transfer options; may return
fullText:
The list of Purdue football players exploring their options in the NCAA transfer portal will include one of the team’s most decorated players. 

IndyStar confirmed safety Dillon Thieneman entered his name in the portal. A report from On3’s Pete Nakos earlier said the Westfield grad intended to do so.

According to a source, Thieneman is open to returning to the Boilermakers, pending the outcome of the ongoing coaching search. 

While the portal officially opens Monday, players whose team undergoes a coaching change can enter from the date of that separation. Players can withdraw from the portal and remain with their teams. 

Purdue coach Hot Board 2.0: What's the latest intel?

More: Former Purdue star, Super Bowl champ enlisted to help Boilers' NIL efforts

It also makes sense for players to enter the portal to gauge their value in the name, image and likeness marketplace. Other teams are not supposed to contact players until they have entered their names in the portal. 

Thieneman was a freshman All-American in 2023, coach Ryan Walters’ first season. His six interceptions were tied for third in the nation. While he did not have any interceptions in the recently completed season, he led Purdue in tackles for the second straight season with 104 with six pass breakups and one sack. 

Thieneman became the highest-profile Boilermaker to enter the portal thus far. Quarterback Ryan Browne entered on Tuesday and also left open the possibility of withdrawing and staying at Purdue. 

Athletic director Mike Bobinski said Monday the coaching search could conclude in a week to 10 days — a timeline in part dictated by the full opening of the portal on Monday.

headline: Indiana women's basketball erases double-digit deficit to edge Southern Indiana
fullText:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana women's basketball might have saved its season on Wednesday night with the kind of defensive intensity that coach Teri Moren wants to define her program.

The Hoosiers (5-3) won their first-ever meeting against Southern Indiana, 67-63, on Wednesday night by holding the Screaming Eagles without any points for 5-plus minutes in the fourth quarter and just 21 points in the second half to overcome a double-digit deficit.

Indiana guard Shay Ciezki, who played much of the second half with four fouls, hit a key 3-pointer from the corner with 25.3 seconds to go. Henna Sandvick came off the bench and came up with a clutch 3-pointer — her first of the season — with 7:02 left.

The Hoosiers' defensive effort helped them overcome a poor shooting performance. They were 35.6% from the field and just 9 of 30 from 3-point range (30%). Yarden Garzon had 14 points, but was 5 of 18 from the floor (2 of 12 from the outside).

Ciezki had a game-high 17 points as one of four IU players in double-digits.

Short-handed Hoosiers shows some fight against Southern Indiana

Indiana erased a 15-point deficit with Moren down to just seven healthy players.

The Hoosiers came into the game without Sydney Parrish (knee) and Lenee Beaumont (knee), who are both out indefinitely. Julianna LaMendola, Parrish’s replacement in the starting lineup, missed much of the second half after suffering an apparent injury two minutes into the third quarter.

LaMendola went back to the locker room for an extended stretch after checking out with 8:05 to go in the quarter. She eventually returned to the bench, but didn't check back in.

Indiana’s focus coming out of halftime was getting the ball inside to 6-foot-3 forward Lilly Meister and leaning on her size advantage. She helped make it a one-possession game with six points during a 10-0 run and Chloe Moore-McNeil tied the score at 44 on a 3-point play with 3:18 left in the third quarter. 

Indiana women’s basketball folds under the pressure in the first half 

Ciezki gestured for a screen — emphatically waving her off hand — while dribbling the ball at the top of the key late in the second quarter. 

No one paid attention to her. 

Ciezki just dribbled aimlessly at the top of the key for nearly 30 seconds until dumping the ball off to Moore-McNeil, who launched an air ball from 3-point range as the shot clock expired. 

Moren threw up her hands in frustration and stormed back down the bench before the shot sailed harmlessly out of bounds. 

Indiana looked dazed and confused from USI’s 2-3 zone and full-court pressure. The Hoosiers had two-extended stretches without a field goal in the half while the Screaming Eagles shot 56.7% from the field in the half and 6 of 8 from 3-point range. 

That came after IU grabbed all the momentum in the going with a 12-2 run to start the game. Southern Indiana tied the score at 17 by the end of the first quarter and went on an extended run in the second quarter with 3-pointers on three consecutive possessions while the Hoosiers went 1 of 13 from the field. 

Indiana also had eight turnovers in the half and was just 5 of 10 from the free-throw line. 

Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek and read all his coverage by clicking here.

headline: Coaches Confidential: IHSAA girls basketball coaches' best advice for rookie counterparts
fullText:
As part of our preseason questionnaires, we granted Central Indiana girls basketball coaches anonymity for the purposes of answering a few questions. 

Here's today’s: What’s the best piece of advice you have for a rookie head coach?

Almost everyone who submitted a preseason questionnaire (61 total) offered a response. Common threads through most of their answers were building a positive culture and putting players first.

“Prioritize culture over X’s and O’s from day one," one coach wrote. "You’ll be a better coach because of it. Everything else will fall in place, but I feel like you have to get the culture piece right. It’s something everyone has to work at daily.”

“Stand on your morals and care more about your win/loss record," wrote another. "Teach life lessons through hoop.”

And from another submission: “What you do has life-long effects."

Many coaches also highlighted the challenges of the job, but encouraged their first-year counterparts to stay the course and believe in themselves. 

"Enjoy the ride, put in the work, believe in yourself and your kids. It can be hard, but it's WORTH IT!”

Another that stood out was the importance of finding joy in both the journey and life outside the gym. 

More: Coaches name their favorite IHSAA players to watch

What we learned from Sneakers for Santa: MVP, most impressive, best teams

From two separate entries:

“Make sure you find time for yourself and your life outside of basketball! Your stress level and ability to lead kids depends on your ability to balance all aspects of your life.”

“Find joy in the journey. It's going to be hard like anything else in the first year, but find joy in the grind. Also find GREAT assistants. They make life a whole lot easier.”

There were so many terrific answers to this prompt. Here are some of the others we received.

∎ “The best piece of advice is to prioritize communication and connection with your players. Build relationships based on trust and respect, and encourage open dialogue. This creates a positive environment where players feel valued and motivated to improve. Additionally, stay adaptable—be willing to adjust your strategies and approaches based on what works best for your team. Focus on growth, both for yourself and your players, and remember to enjoy the journey!”

∎ “Stay organized, communicate clearly with parents and keep things simple early and build upon what your team and players do best.”

∎ “Be confident in your decisions and be a great communicator.”

∎ “No matter what you do or what you say, you can't please everyone. Focus solely on SERVING THE CHILDREN YOU ARE BLESSED TO COACH. Nothing else matters, be what they NEED, do right by the children FIRST. Love them unconditionally and coach them in a way that has a positive impact on their future. If you do this first in all you do, all will be well.”

∎ “It’s hard! But take control early and make them buy into your program. If they don't you can find someone who will and those are players you want to coach. You are developing these girls to become successful people, not just basketball players. What you do has life-long effects.”

∎ “Take each day to build strong relationships with your team. Prioritize teaching the basic fundamentals of the game. Set standards and expectations, hold them accountable in practices and not just on game days.”

∎ “Build healthy relationships with your players and coach each one of them based on who they are. Players will give you everything they have when they know you care about them as a person.”

∎ “Always put the players first, and make sure all of your young ladies take care of business in the classroom as well as on the court.”

∎ “Remember this is the kids’ experience and you will play a major role in whether they judge it as positive or negative.”

∎ “Build the relationship and rapport with your players first over trying to get wins. This will help in so many ways.”

∎ “Keep the girls’ best interest at the forefront when making decisions … at the end of the day it is for THEM!!”

∎ “Invest the time to build relationships with your players.”

∎ “Remember, you are best when you are a ‘servant leader’ for your kids. The girls under your care love playing the game of basketball. Do everything you can to accentuate that love of the game for them.”

∎ “Be patient in the coaching process. Coaching and teaching are the same thing and require us to meet players where they are, then provide the tools for them to grow.”

∎ “Coach Al Rhodes gave me great advice: Build your program top down. Focus on your culture at the varsity level and develop a program of excellence, then it can be passed down to the underclassmen and developed at the lower levels with the example at the varsity level.”

∎ “Surround yourself with great assistant coaches. Be involved with your feeder program. Have fun and enjoy the journey!!!!!!”

∎ “There is so much more to being a head coach than the X's and O’s, so you must be organized and understand the rules, regulations, and expectations of your athletic department. Hire great loyal staff throughout your program and continue to study the game.”

∎ “Delegate and surround yourself with people you trust and who will hold you accountable.”

∎ “Build your youth program, work hard at preparation, build relationships, stay true to yourself and your core principles.”

∎ “Give yourself a little time to establish yourself as you build your program. Work hard, give grace and be clear about what you are building. Stay the course when you get any pushback or negativity. Create partnerships with your parents.”

∎ “Decide on who you want to be as a coach and then make decisions through that lens. Keep a wide view of the program.”

∎ “Be YOU! Don’t try to be someone else that you think you should be or should be coaching like.”

∎ “Define success on your own terms. Don't let someone else tell you what success means.”

∎ “Give yourself some grace and always stay true to your values and principles.”

∎ “Praise and blame are all the same. You are never as good as they say you are and you are also never as bad as they say you are. When you come to the gym, care about every kid, family, coach and worker. When it comes down to it, other people walk in solely to support or see one or two people. Keep that in perspective.”

∎ “Find a mentor and use them to your advantage!”

∎ “Year 1 is year 0, Year 2 is year 1, Year 3 is year 2 — trust yourself and stay the course.”

∎ “Stay focused on what really matters, the positives that come out of every practice and game. Find a way to fix one negative a day.”

∎ “1. Outwork, don’t just compete 2. Keep the main thing the main thing 3. Build your village 4. Trust the process. 5. Be consistently consistent. 6. Know the difference between “Fool's Gold” and “Real Gold.” These combined with adding your energy and passion - trust yourself and appreciate the journey!”

∎ “There are going to be ups and downs in every season. Make sure you enjoy the journey. Believe in what you do. There will be a LOT of opinions out there, but nobody knows your team like you do, believe in what you do.”

∎ “Control what you can control. Regardless of wins and losses, block the noise and coach your players with integrity and teach them life lessons beyond basketball. You will never be able to please everyone.”

∎ “Enjoy every minute of the position you have.”
